dimension: Coordinator identity + runtime gating (how "coordinator" is identified and what it actually gates in code)
summary: "Coordinator" in c2c is NOT a first-class identity in the messaging core — it is three loosely-coupled things that mostly DON'T agree at runtime. (1) An env flag `C2C_COORDINATOR=1` is the ONLY thing that gates code, and it gates exactly four narrow surfaces: a privilege bypass on `from`-alias spoofing in `c2c send` / `c2c rooms send`, a hard requirement for the `coord cherry-pick` utility, an exemption from the soft worktree-mismatch broker warning, and the destructive-git-op shell shims (commit/reset/switch/checkout/rebase bypass). (2) A role-file `coordinator: true` field whose ONLY runtime effect is to propagate `C2C_COORDINATOR=1` into a managed session's env at launch (c2c_start.ml:4400) — it is a convenience funnel into mechanism (1). (3) The alias string `"coordinator1"` which is purely a hardcoded DEFAULT/FALLBACK for permission-supervisor and DM-routing, never a privilege check. The actual messaging core (broker enqueue/drain, register, list, rooms join/send/history, send_all, schedules, memory) has ZERO coordinator concept — room deletion ACL is creator-based (`created_by`), permission approval is a caller-supplied `supervisors[]` list, and the registration `role` string is cosmetic envelope metadata that gates nothing. The planned `swarm_config_coordinator_alias` helper does NOT exist (only a stale comment references it); `coordinator1` is hardcoded in ~8 distinct default sites.

coupling_points.title: C2C_COORDINATOR=1 bypasses from-alias spoofing guard in `c2c send`
coupling_points.what_it_does: validate_from_override returns immediately (no ownership check) when is_coordinator() is true, letting the caller send a DM stamped as ANY other registered alias. Without it, sending as an alias registered to a different session is refused (exit 1).
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:105-147 (is_coordinator at :106 reads `Sys.getenv_opt "C2C_COORDINATOR" = Some "1"`; bypass at :109)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: This is a relay-on-behalf capability, not an identity. For a solo/flat mesh it is simply never set, so the guard is always active and you can only send as yourself — which is the correct default. Keep the bypass as an opt-in operator escape hatch (rename to e.g. C2C_RELAY_ANY_ALIAS=1 to drop the 'coordinator' framing); the core send path needs no coordinator concept.

coupling_points.title: C2C_COORDINATOR=1 bypasses from-alias spoofing guard in `c2c rooms send` (duplicated logic)
coupling_points.what_it_does: Identical spoofing-guard bypass for room sends; the check is inlined (copy of c2c.ml logic) because c2c_rooms.ml does not depend on c2c.ml.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_rooms.ml:32 (`is_coordinator = Sys.getenv_opt "C2C_COORDINATOR" = Some "1"`), bypass at :36
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Same as the send guard — never set in solo/flat mode, so the guard always holds. The duplicated block should be factored into one shared helper (C2c_cli_auth.validate_from_override is referenced in a comment as the canonical one) regardless of the role question.

coupling_points.title: C2C_COORDINATOR=1 is a HARD precondition for `c2c coord cherry-pick`
coupling_points.what_it_does: run_coord_cherry_pick exits 1 immediately unless C2C_COORDINATOR is exactly "1". This is the only place the env var is a hard gate (code refuses to run without it).
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_coord.ml:202-209 (matches getenv; eprintf + exit 1 on None/""/other)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: This is a structured-team deploy utility (cherry-pick peer SHAs to master + install + DM authors), wholly outside the messaging core. A solo user never invokes it. It can stay as an opt-in team feature; the gate is a self-imposed safety lock, not a messaging dependency. The messaging core does not link against it.

coupling_points.title: C2C_COORDINATOR=1 exempts sender from broker worktree-mismatch warning
coupling_points.what_it_does: check_worktree_mismatch returns early (no WORKTREE_MISMATCH log) when C2C_COORDINATOR=1, on the theory the coordinator legitimately runs from the main tree. This is a SOFT warn-only path — it only writes a broker.log event, never blocks a message.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:1129-1134 (`if Sys.getenv_opt "C2C_COORDINATOR" = Some "1" then ()`)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: This is the ONLY coordinator env check inside the broker, and it only suppresses a log line. The whole Hardening-B mismatch guard is a swarm-discipline feature (detecting main-tree contamination) irrelevant to solo/flat use. In a flat mesh the expected-cwd file simply does not exist (guard no-ops at :1136). Removing the env check entirely would only mean coordinators get a harmless extra log line.

coupling_points.title: Role-file `coordinator: true` -> propagates C2C_COORDINATOR=1 at launch
coupling_points.what_it_does: When a managed session's role file has `coordinator: true`, c2c start appends `C2C_COORDINATOR=1` to the child env. This is the ONLY runtime consumer of the role.coordinator field.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_start.ml:4396-4402 (`Some r when r.C2c_role.coordinator = Some true -> Array.append env [| "C2C_COORDINATOR=1" |]`); field defined ocaml/c2c_role.ml:18, parsed :267
coupling_points.decouple_approach: This is pure sugar: it converts a role-file boolean into the env flag, funneling into the four env-var couplings above. A solo user launching with no role file (agent_role = None) never triggers it. Decouple by treating it as just one more way to set an operator opt-in capability; the field can be dropped entirely and operators set C2C_COORDINATOR in extra_env if they want the team behaviors.

coupling_points.title: Role-file `role_class: coordinator` drives pmodel + heartbeat + auto-join, NOT privileges
coupling_points.what_it_does: role_class is a free-form string bucket used for (a) pmodel resolution, (b) gating which managed heartbeats apply (should_heartbeat_apply_to_role), (c) auto-join role-room mapping. 'coordinator' is just one possible value with no special code path — 'coder'/'reviewer' are treated identically.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_role.ml:16 (role_class field); ocaml/c2c_start.ml:939-949 (heartbeat role_classes filter), :2914-2923 (auto-join role-room via role_class_to_room); role_class_to_room at c2c_role.ml:564
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Fully role-agnostic by construction — it is a generic class label, not a coordinator gate. No change needed for solo/flat: unset role_class falls back to 'default'. The string 'coordinator' here is incidental.

coupling_points.title: Registration `role` string is cosmetic envelope metadata, gates nothing
coupling_points.what_it_does: The `register` tool accepts an optional `role` ("coordinator/reviewer/agent/user"). It is stored on the registration and used only for envelope attribution display. The broker never branches on it.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_mcp_helpers.ml:52-54 (field doc 'gates nothing'); ocaml/c2c_mcp.ml:36 (tool prop); ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:1970-1972 (effective_role just preserved on re-register). Grep for reg.role consumption in broker found only storage, no gating.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already role-agnostic — it is free-text decoration. Solo users omit it. No coupling to remove.

coupling_points.title: Hardcoded `coordinator1` as permission-supervisor default (multiple clients)
coupling_points.what_it_does: When no supervisors[]/authorizers[] are configured in .c2c/repo.json and no sidecar override, the permission-approval flow defaults the supervisor/reviewer alias to the literal 'coordinator1'. Applies to: opencode plugin resolveSupervisors fallback, kimi approval hook fallback, kimi-hook `--reviewer` CLI default, and the doctor display default.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_opencode_plugin_embedded.ml:105 (`return ["coordinator1"]`); ocaml/cli/c2c_kimi_hook.ml:230 (`AUTHORIZERS+=("coordinator1")`); ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:6509 (`opt string "coordinator1"`), :1952 / :1959 (doctor default text)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: The approval mechanism itself is role-AGNOSTIC: it resolves whatever alias list (supervisors[]/authorizers[]) the requester or repo.json supplies, checks liveness/DnD/idle (Broker.resolve_authorizers, c2c_broker.ml:4151), and validates replies against the caller-supplied supervisors list (c2c_pending_reply_handlers.ml:156). 'coordinator1' is purely the last-resort default when nothing is configured. For solo/flat: permission approval is itself an opt-in structured-team feature (no approval gate exists unless a client wires the PreToolUse hook). Replace the hardcoded default with 'none configured -> no forwarding' or a config-driven helper; the irreducible core (resolve-from-a-list) needs no coordinator.

coupling_points.title: Hardcoded `coordinator1` as DM-routing fallback (cherry-pick, agent refine, worktree gc)
coupling_points.what_it_does: Several utilities self-DM or fall back to 'coordinator1' when they cannot resolve a target: coord cherry-pick self-DMs coordinator1 for unknown commit authors; `c2c agent refine --agent-mode` DMs coordinator1 when C2C_MCP_REPLY_TO is unset; worktree gc --ask-authors uses coordinator1 as the our_alias fallback. Email->alias table also hardcodes coordinator1@c2c.im.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_coord.ml:127 (`c2c send coordinator1`), :67 (email map); ocaml/cli/c2c_agent.ml:721-722 (reply-to fallback); ocaml/cli/c2c_worktree.ml:1887 (gc fallback)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: All are fallbacks in team-tooling, not the messaging core. Each should read a configurable coordinator/owner alias (the planned-but-absent swarm_config_coordinator_alias) or degrade gracefully (skip the DM / use the current alias). Solo users never hit these paths. No hard dependency.

coupling_points.title: coord_fallthrough scheduler — broker-side per-DM escalation chain
coupling_points.what_it_does: A broker-internal scheduler (started in c2c_mcp_server_inner.ml:548) escalates unanswered permission DMs through a config-driven `coord_chain` of aliases, then broadcasts to a room. Despite the name, it uses VERBATIM aliases from config (no role indirection) and is a no-op when coord_chain is empty (the default).
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/coord_fallthrough.ml:20 ('verbatim aliases in coord_chain (no role indirection)'), :95 (`chain = [] then No_action`); config thunk swarm_config_coord_chain defaults to [] at c2c_start.ml:745-753; started at ocaml/server/c2c_mcp_server_inner.ml:548
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already role-agnostic and OFF by default (empty chain). It is an opt-in redundancy feature layered on the permission flow. Solo/flat users leave coord_chain unset and the scheduler does nothing each tick. The 'coord' naming is cosmetic; the mechanism is a generic alias-escalation list.

coupling_points.title: git-shim / pre-commit hook destructive-op guards bypass via C2C_COORDINATOR=1
coupling_points.what_it_does: Shell shims refuse `git commit` on main/master, `git reset --hard` (commit-loss), branch switch/checkout/rebase in the MAIN tree for non-coordinators; C2C_COORDINATOR=1 bypasses all of them. These are git-workflow discipline guards, entirely outside the c2c messaging binary.
coupling_points.evidence: git-shim.sh:52 (`COORDINATOR="${C2C_COORDINATOR:-0}"`), :146/:167/:319 (guards); .c2c/hooks/pre-commit.sh:8 (branch guard), scripts/setup-pre-push-hook.sh:6 (push guard)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: These are opt-in installed guards (c2c install self/git-shim/git-hook) for shared-tree swarm discipline. A solo user simply does not install them, or sets C2C_COORDINATOR=1. They have zero coupling to message delivery. Keep as a structured-team add-on.

coupling_points.title: swarm_config_coordinator_alias / swarm_config_social_room helpers DO NOT EXIST
coupling_points.what_it_does: CLAUDE.md and a c2c_start.ml comment reference these helpers as the canonical way to look up the coordinator alias / social room. In current code they are unimplemented — only the comment exists. 'swarm-lounge' and 'coordinator1' are therefore hardcoded at every use site rather than resolved through a config helper.
coupling_points.evidence: Grep across ocaml/**/*.ml: the only hit for swarm_config_coordinator_alias is the comment at c2c_start.ml:661; no `let swarm_config_coordinator_alias`. social_room default 'swarm-lounge' hardcoded e.g. c2c_start.ml:739, c2c_broker.ml:4064.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: The absence is the opportunity: implement swarm_config_coordinator_alias / swarm_config_social_room as config thunks (mirroring swarm_config_restart_intro at c2c_start.ml:710) returning Option/empty when unconfigured, and route the ~8 hardcoded 'coordinator1' default sites through it. Then a solo user with no config gets 'no coordinator', and the team-feature defaults become opt-in config rather than baked-in literals.

irreducible_core: Broker enqueue_message / drain_inbox: pure alias->alias delivery, no role/coordinator concept (c2c_broker.ml). Message envelope is from/to/content only.
register / list / whoami: identity is (session_id, alias); no role required to register or be listed. role string is optional cosmetic metadata that gates nothing (c2c_mcp_helpers.ml:52-54).

Rooms (join_room/send_room/room_history/my_rooms/list_rooms/leave_room): membership and creator-based ACL only. delete_room authorizes on created_by, not on any coordinator status (c2c_broker.ml:3521-3545).
send_all (1:N broadcast) and rooms (N:N): topology primitives with no privilege gate.
Native scheduling (schedule_set/list/rm) and per-agent memory: per-alias, role-agnostic.

from-alias spoofing guard DEFAULT (the part WITHOUT the bypass): 'you may only send as your own registered alias' is the correct, role-free invariant for a flat mesh (c2c.ml:108-147, the else branch).

Permission-approval mechanism MINUS the hardcoded default: resolve-first-available-from-a-supplied-alias-list + reply-validated-against-that-list (Broker.resolve_authorizers c2c_broker.ml:4151; c2c_pending_reply_handlers.ml:156) is inherently role-agnostic; only the fallback alias is coordinator-flavored.
simplification_opportunities: C2C_COORDINATOR is overloaded across three unrelated concerns: (a) relay-as-another-alias capability, (b) cherry-pick utility lock, (c) git-discipline-guard bypass. Split into named capability flags (e.g. C2C_RELAY_ANY_ALIAS, leave git-shim with its own bypass) so the messaging binary stops conflating 'I am the coordinator' with 'I may send as someone else'. The send/rooms-send bypass is the only one that touches the messaging core.

Implement the absent swarm_config_coordinator_alias / swarm_config_social_room config thunks (mirror swarm_config_restart_intro, c2c_start.ml:710) and route the ~8 hardcoded 'coordinator1' / 'swarm-lounge' default sites through them, returning empty/None when unconfigured. Result: zero coordinator literals fire for a solo/flat user.

The from-alias spoofing-guard logic is duplicated verbatim between c2c.ml:108-147 and c2c_rooms.ml:32-73. Factor into one shared C2c_cli_auth helper; the bypass-condition then lives in exactly one place and is trivial to make config-driven.

The role-file `coordinator: true` -> C2C_COORDINATOR=1 funnel (c2c_start.ml:4400) can be dropped: operators who want the env flag in a managed session can set it via extra_env, removing a redundant identity surface. role_class already carries the non-privilege team-bucket semantics.

The broker worktree-mismatch C2C_COORDINATOR exemption (c2c_broker.ml:1134) only suppresses a log line; it could be removed outright, eliminating the broker's single env-coordinator check and making the broker fully role-agnostic.

Make the permission/approval surface explicitly opt-in: when no supervisors[]/authorizers[] is configured, forward to nobody (or no-op the gate) instead of defaulting to 'coordinator1'. This makes the feature invisible to solo users and structured-only by configuration.
open_questions: Should the relay-as-another-alias capability (the only coordinator coupling in the messaging core) be retained at all in a flat-mesh design, or is 'always send as yourself' acceptable, dropping the bypass entirely? It is currently the load-bearing reason C2C_COORDINATOR exists in c2c.ml/c2c_rooms.ml.

The permission-approval flow (kimi PreToolUse hook, opencode permission.ask) is a genuine structured-team feature with real broker state (pending_permissions, coord_fallthrough scheduler). Is it in-scope to keep as opt-in, or should it move out of the core binary entirely? It pulls in the largest coordinator-flavored surface (supervisors[], authorizers[], coord_chain, fallthrough scheduler).

If swarm_config_coordinator_alias is implemented, what should it return for a solo user with no config — None (and each call-site degrades) or the current-session alias? The DM-routing fallbacks (cherry-pick self-DM, agent refine reply-to) need a defined no-coordinator behavior.

Role-file `coordinator: true` and registration `role` string both exist but neither is the privilege source (the env flag is). Is the intent to eventually make role authoritative, or keep env as the single gate? Right now they can disagree (a session can have role=coordinator metadata without C2C_COORDINATOR=1, or vice versa).

The git-shim/hooks bypass shares the C2C_COORDINATOR name but is a separate enforcement domain (shell, not the binary). Should it keep the shared name (so one flag flips both) or get its own, to avoid a messaging-relay grant accidentally also unlocking destructive git ops?

dimension: Git integration (destructive-op guard shim, pre-commit/pre-push hooks, attribution shim, coord cherry-pick, kimi approval hook) and its coupling to the coordinator/role concept
summary: The git guard surface is almost entirely keyed on STRUCTURE + a single ENV VAR, not on role. The pre-reset shim (`git-shim.sh`, installed as `git-pre-reset`) decides "guard or not" purely on `[ -d .git ]` (main tree) vs `[ -f .git ]` (worktree) — see git-shim.sh:62-74 — and bypasses on `C2C_COORDINATOR=1` (git-shim.sh:52,146,167,189,237,286). It never reads a role file. The pre-commit (`.c2c/hooks/pre-commit.sh`) and pre-push (`scripts/git-hooks/pre-push`) hooks branch-gate on `master`/`main` with the same `C2C_COORDINATOR=1` env bypass — again no role. The ONLY place "role" enters git is c2c_start.ml:4396-4402, which auto-exports `C2C_COORDINATOR=1` when the role file has a `coordinator: true` boolean field. CRITICAL FINDING: no role file in the repo sets that field — `Cairn-Vigil.md` (coordinator1) has `role_class: coordinator` but NOT `coordinator:`, and `parse_bool(find "coordinator")` (c2c_role.ml:267) therefore returns `None`. So the role→env link is effectively dead in practice; coordinator privilege is set manually via the env var. That means the guards are ALREADY ~role-agnostic in code. The kimi PreToolUse approval hook is the one genuinely role-flavored piece (forwards to `supervisors[]`/`coordinator1`), but it is a separate opt-in kimi-only surface, not part of the destructive-op guard. The whole shim system is itself opt-in via `git_attribution` in `.c2c/config.toml` (defaults true; c2c_start.ml:520-548) and only active for managed `c2c start` sessions whose PATH is prepended with the shim dir.

coupling_points.title: Pre-reset/branch-guard shim keys on worktree-vs-maintree + C2C_COORDINATOR env, NOT role
coupling_points.evidence: git-shim.sh:62-74 (is_main_tree=[-d .git], is_worktree_branch=[-f .git]); git-shim.sh:52 (COORDINATOR=${C2C_COORDINATOR:-0}); refusals all gated `is_main_tree && [ "$COORDINATOR" != "1" ]` at git-shim.sh:146,167,189,237,286
coupling_points.what_it_does: Refuses reset --hard (behind-HEAD), commit on main/master, switch/checkout <branch>, rebase <upstream> in the MAIN tree only; worktrees (.git is a file) are never guarded; C2C_COORDINATOR=1 bypasses everything.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already structural. The word 'coordinator' in the env-var name and messages is the only role flavor — purely cosmetic. Rename C2C_COORDINATOR to C2C_GIT_GUARD_BYPASS (or honor a generic --force/profile) and the guard is fully role-agnostic with zero behavior change. A solo user in the main tree on master would hit the commit refusal, so for solo/flat-mesh the guard must default OFF when no team profile is configured.

coupling_points.title: git_attribution config gate makes the WHOLE shim system opt-in (and is role-agnostic)
coupling_points.evidence: c2c_start.ml:520-548 (repo_config_git_attribution reads `git_attribution` from .c2c/config.toml, DEFAULTS TRUE when absent); c2c_start.ml:2935 (enable_git_shim = repo_config_git_attribution ()); c2c_start.ml:3003-3007,3038-3050 (only when enabled is the shim dir prepended to PATH)
coupling_points.what_it_does: If git_attribution is false (or attribution disabled), neither the attribution shim nor the pre-reset guard is on PATH for managed sessions — so NONE of the destructive-op guards fire. This is the master opt-out switch and it is keyed on a repo config bool, not a role.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: This IS the opt-in safety-profile hook the north-star wants. Split it: keep `git_attribution` (commit author identity) separate from a new `git_guards` (destructive-op refusals) so a solo user can keep attribution but disable guards. Default guards OFF for unconfigured repos; teams turn them on.

coupling_points.title: Role→C2C_COORDINATOR auto-injection is the ONLY role link — and it is currently a no-op
coupling_points.evidence: c2c_start.ml:4396-4402 (`Some r when r.C2c_role.coordinator = Some true -> append C2C_COORDINATOR=1`); c2c_role.ml:267 (coordinator = parse_bool (find "coordinator")); .c2c/roles/builtins/Cairn-Vigil.md:1-13 has role_class: coordinator + alias: coordinator1 but NO `coordinator:` field; repo-wide grep for `coordinator:` boolean across .c2c/roles/ returns empty
coupling_points.what_it_does: Intended to derive coordinator privilege from the role file so coordinator1's managed session bypasses guards automatically. In practice no role sets the `coordinator:` boolean, so the branch never fires and C2C_COORDINATOR must be set manually.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: This is the single hard coupling between roles and git guards, and it is already dormant. To go fully role-agnostic: delete the c2c_start.ml:4396-4402 block and the `coordinator` field from c2c_role.ml/.mli; let C2C_COORDINATOR (or its renamed successor) be set only by explicit env / a per-session safety-profile flag. No code path other than this one reads a role to influence git behavior.

coupling_points.title: pre-commit coordinator gate (.c2c/hooks/pre-commit.sh) — branch-keyed + env bypass, no role
coupling_points.evidence: .c2c/hooks/pre-commit.sh:5-13 (BRANCH=symbolic-ref; PROTECTED=^(master|main)$; blocks unless C2C_COORDINATOR=1); installed by c2c install git-hook (c2c_setup.ml:2033-2060) copying .c2c/hooks/pre-commit.sh -> .git/hooks/pre-commit
coupling_points.what_it_does: Refuses any commit on master/main unless C2C_COORDINATOR=1. Pure branch check + env bypass.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Identical pattern to the shim: structural branch check + cosmetic env name. For solo/flat-mesh, don't install this hook by default, or make the protected-branch set + bypass token configurable. The `--no-verify` git escape already exists as a per-commit override.

coupling_points.title: pre-push coordinator gate (scripts/git-hooks/pre-push) — repo-URL match + branch + env bypass
coupling_points.evidence: scripts/git-hooks/pre-push:38-54 (is_c2c_repo by URL match clankercode/c2c, :src/c2c, /c2c); :51-54 (C2C_COORDINATOR=1 bypass); :57-77 (reject if local_ref==refs/heads/master); installed by just install-git-hooks (justfile:288-297) symlink + recompute_git_hook_artifacts (c2c_uninstall.ml:470-471)
coupling_points.what_it_does: Rejects push to origin/master for the c2c repo specifically unless C2C_COORDINATOR=1. The 'coordinator gate' is just: this-repo + master-branch + no-bypass-env. No role read.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: The repo-URL hardcoding (clankercode/c2c) is project-specific, not role-specific. For a generic c2c, key the gate on a configurable protected-remote/branch list in repo config, default OFF. A solo user pushing their own repo should never see this; today they would IF they happen to install the hook and their remote URL ends in /c2c.

coupling_points.title: Two different pre-commit hooks compete for .git/hooks/pre-commit (install-path divergence)
coupling_points.evidence: c2c install git-hook writes .c2c/hooks/pre-commit.sh (coordinator gate) -> .git/hooks/pre-commit (c2c_setup.ml:2033-2059); just install-git-hooks symlinks scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit (bun plugin syntax check, scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit:1-40) -> same .git/hooks/pre-commit (justfile:293-296). uninstall is_c2c_hook matches BOTH (c2c_uninstall.ml:285-298)
coupling_points.what_it_does: `c2c install git-hook` and `just install-git-hooks` install DIFFERENT scripts to the same path. The coordinator-gate pre-commit and the plugin-syntax pre-commit are mutually exclusive depending on which installer ran last. Only one role-relevant (the coordinator gate).
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Not a role coupling per se, but a footgun that obscures the coupling. Consolidate: one pre-commit that does syntax-check always + optional protected-branch gate behind config. Removes the coordinator-gate variant from the default path entirely for solo users.

coupling_points.title: Broker worktree-mismatch guard exempts C2C_COORDINATOR (soft-warn only, not a git op)
coupling_points.evidence: c2c_broker.ml:1129-1134 (check_worktree_mismatch skips when C2C_COORDINATOR=1; logs WORKTREE_MISMATCH otherwise, soft warn); comment 'coordinator may run from main tree'
coupling_points.what_it_does: On message send, logs (does not block) if sender's registration cwd != expected-cwd; coordinator env exempts. Advisory telemetry, not enforcement.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Drop the coordinator exemption or gate it on the same generic bypass token. Since it is warn-only it is harmless for solo users (no expected-cwd file -> early return at c2c_broker.ml:1136). Fully role-agnostic if the env name is generalized.

coupling_points.title: coord-cherry-pick requires C2C_COORDINATOR=1 (hard env gate, not role)
coupling_points.evidence: c2c_coord.ml:202-210 (run_coord_cherry_pick errors out unless C2C_COORDINATOR=1); tests/test_coord_cherry_pick.sh:50-56 (gate test); c2c_coord.ml:11 comment 'coordinator-only (check C2C_COORDINATOR env)'
coupling_points.what_it_does: The coordinator cherry-pick/land helper hard-refuses unless C2C_COORDINATOR=1. This is a deliberately coordinator-scoped convenience tool, gated on env not role file.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: This is a structured-team feature by design; for a solo/flat mesh it simply isn't used. Keep as opt-in tooling behind the env/profile; no role read to remove. A solo user never invokes `c2c coord cherry-pick`.

coupling_points.title: kimi PreToolUse approval hook forwards to supervisors[]/coordinator1 (the one genuinely role-shaped git-adjacent gate)
coupling_points.evidence: scripts/c2c-kimi-approval-hook.sh:45 (REVIEWER=${C2C_KIMI_APPROVAL_REVIEWER:-coordinator1}); :74-88 (git push/commit/reset/etc require approval, read-only git allowed); embedded copy resolves supervisors[] from .c2c/repo.json (c2c-kimi-approval-hook.sh:112-118 comment); repo.json supervisors=[coordinator1]

coupling_points.decouple_approach: Default reviewer to self-approve / no-op when no supervisors[] configured, so a solo kimi user is never gated. The hardcoded `coordinator1` default (line 45) is the only role assumption; make it require an explicit supervisor list with empty-list => allow.

coupling_points.title: Attribution shim ('git' wrapper) sets author identity — fully role-agnostic
coupling_points.evidence: c2c_start.ml:1781-1824 (write_git_shim_atomic writes 'git' that exports C2C_GIT_SHIM_ACTIVE then execs git-pre-reset); c2c_start.ml:2961-2974 (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL=<alias>@c2c.im set per managed session)
coupling_points.what_it_does: Stamps commits with the session alias as author/committer. Keyed on alias, not role. The 'git' shim simply delegates to git-pre-reset (the guard).
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already alias-keyed, role-agnostic. Works identically for any peer in a flat mesh. No change needed beyond decoupling it from the guard delegation if guards are made separately opt-out.

irreducible_core: worktree-vs-maintree structural detection ([-d .git] vs [-f .git], git-shim.sh:62-74) — a clean, role-free signal that worktrees are safe and the shared main tree is the thing worth protecting
per-alias commit attribution via GIT_AUTHOR_*/the 'git' shim (c2c_start.ml:1781-1824, 2961-2974) — identity, not authority; works for any peer
the reset --hard behind-HEAD commit-loss detection (target_behind_head, git-shim.sh:80-94) — a genuinely useful guard for ANY user, solo or team, with no role semantics
the runaway-spawn / recursion circuit breaker (git-shim.sh:43-50) — pure safety, role-irrelevant
a single generic bypass token (currently C2C_COORDINATOR) — useful as an escape hatch for any user, just mis-named after a role
git_attribution config gate as the master opt-in switch (c2c_start.ml:520-548) — the right shape for an opt-in safety profile, just currently conflating attribution and guards
simplification_opportunities: Remove the dormant role->env link: delete c2c_start.ml:4396-4402 and the `coordinator` field from c2c_role.ml:267/.mli:8 — no role file uses it, so this is dead code that falsely implies roles drive git guards.

Rename C2C_COORDINATOR to a role-neutral C2C_GIT_GUARD_BYPASS (alias the old name for compat) across git-shim.sh, .c2c/hooks/pre-commit.sh, scripts/git-hooks/pre-push, c2c_broker.ml:1134 — the guards become self-evidently role-agnostic.

Split the single `git_attribution` config into `git_attribution` (identity) + `git_guards` (destructive-op refusals), defaulting guards OFF for unconfigured/solo repos so a solo user committing on master in the main tree is never refused.

Make the protected-branch set and protected-remote URL configurable instead of hardcoding master/main and clankercode/c2c (scripts/git-hooks/pre-push:40) — removes the project-specific assumption that breaks generic/solo use.

Reconcile the two competing pre-commit installers (c2c install git-hook vs just install-git-hooks) into one hook: always-on plugin syntax check + optional protected-branch gate behind config; drops the coordinator-gate variant from the default solo path.
Default the kimi approval reviewer to no-op when supervisors[] is empty (scripts/c2c-kimi-approval-hook.sh:45) so a solo kimi user is never blocked waiting on a non-existent coordinator.

Delete the stale C2C_GIT_SHIM_MAIN_TREE env var from test_git_shim.sh (it is set by the test but ignored by the current shim, which is purely structural) to avoid implying an env-driven main-tree override exists.
open_questions: Was the `coordinator: true` role field ever wired, or is it aspirational? coordinator1's Cairn-Vigil.md uses role_class:coordinator but not the boolean — is c2c_start.ml:4400 a planned-but-never-completed feature, and does any out-of-repo/personal role file set it?

For a solo user, should the main-tree commit refusal default ON (forcing worktree discipline) or OFF (frictionless)? The north-star says zero coordinator concept, which argues OFF-by-default with opt-in for teams.

Should the generic bypass be an env var, a `--force` flag per-op, or a persisted per-session safety-profile (e.g. .c2c/config.toml git_guards = off)? A profile is more discoverable than an env var for solo users.

The pre-push hook's c2c-repo detection hardcodes clankercode/c2c and any URL ending /c2c — does this accidentally gate unrelated solo repos whose path ends in /c2c? (scripts/git-hooks/pre-push:40 matches *"/c2c")
Are the kimi approval supervisors[] the same concept as the (dead) coordinator role field, and should they be unified into one 'who can authorize' config that defaults to self/empty for solo?

dimension: Roles, role files, and role/coordinator coupling in c2c
summary: A "role" in c2c is a markdown file with YAML frontmatter living at `.c2c/roles/<name>.md` (canonical) or a client-native agents dir, parsed by `C2c_role.parse_string`/`parse_file` (ocaml/c2c_role.ml:249-298) into a record of ~22 fields. Roles are entirely OPT-IN already: `c2c start <client>` only applies a role when `--agent <name>` is passed or a role file matching the instance name happens to exist; with neither, it launches a flat full-capability peer with `agent_name=None`, `role_pmodel_override=None` (ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:9633-9655). Almost every role field is advisory rendering input (description, role, pronouns, model, opencode/claude/codex/kimi tool sub-tables, compatible_clients, required_capabilities). Only `coordinator: true` gates real capability: it propagates `C2C_COORDINATOR=1` into the launch env (ocaml/c2c_start.ml:4396-4402), which is the single bypass key for the destructive-git-op guard (git-shim.sh:52, 146, 167, 189, 237), the coord-cherry-pick subcommand (ocaml/cli/c2c_coord.ml:202-209), send-as-another-alias relay (ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:105-147), and the worktree-mismatch warn (ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:1133). Crucially the tier-command-hiding and the broker itself are role-AGNOSTIC: tier filtering keys on `C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID` presence (ocaml/cli/c2c_commands.ml:113-120), and broker registration treats `role` as optional display-only metadata (ocaml/c2c_mcp.ml:208-214). The coordinator-as-a-named-peer (`coordinator1`) and the social room (`swarm-lounge`) are hardcoded strings in install/hook/template paths but are pure conventions/defaults, overridable via config. Making roles fully opt-in is essentially already done at the broker/mesh layer; the residual coupling is the `coordinator: true`→`C2C_COORDINATOR` capability bypass (which is independently env-settable, so role is not load-bearing for it) and a scatter of hardcoded `coordinator1`/`swarm-lounge` default strings.

coupling_points.title: Role file format + on-disk location
coupling_points.what_it_does: A role is a YAML-frontmatter + markdown-body file. Canonical path `.c2c/roles/<name>.md`; falls back to client-native dirs (.claude/agents, .opencode/agents, .codex/agents, .kimi/agents/<name>/). Parsed into a 22-field record; rendered per-client (claude/codex/opencode/kimi) by dedicated renderers.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_role.ml:3-31 (type t), :539-562 (canonical_roles_dir, client_agent_dir, resolve_agent_path), :249-298 (parse), :397-533 (renderers)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already decoupled — a role file is consumed only when explicitly requested; no broker/mesh subsystem reads role files.

coupling_points.title: Role is opt-in at launch: no-role path launches a flat full-capability peer
coupling_points.what_it_does: cmd_start applies a role only when `--agent <name>` is given OR a role file named after the instance exists. With neither, the `else` branch returns (kickoff, alias_opt, None, None, None) — agent_name=None, role_pmodel=None — and the session launches as an unstructured peer.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:9456-9655 (the big match; no-role else at :9633-9655 returns Nones)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: This IS the opt-in behavior. A solo/flat user simply runs `c2c start <client>` with no role file. Works today.

coupling_points.title: `coordinator: true` role field → C2C_COORDINATOR=1 env (THE capability gate)
coupling_points.what_it_does: At launch, if the loaded role has `coordinator = Some true`, c2c appends `C2C_COORDINATOR=1` to the managed client's env. This is the only role field that grants elevated privilege rather than just affecting rendering.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_start.ml:4232-4240 (load role early), :4396-4402 (propagate C2C_COORDINATOR=1); field defined ocaml/c2c_role.ml:18, parsed :267
coupling_points.decouple_approach: C2C_COORDINATOR is already independently settable as an env var (operator export, `C2C_COORDINATOR=1 git push`). The role field is just a convenience to auto-set it. Removing the field changes a default (coordinator must set env manually) but breaks no code. For a flat mesh, simply never set the field; no agent gets the bypass and everyone uses worktrees.

coupling_points.title: C2C_COORDINATOR bypasses the destructive-git-op guard (pre-reset shim)
coupling_points.what_it_does: git-shim.sh (installed as `git-pre-reset`) refuses `reset --hard <behind-HEAD>`, `commit` on main/master, `switch <branch>`, `checkout <branch>`, `rebase <upstream>` in the MAIN TREE for non-coordinators. `C2C_COORDINATOR=1` bypasses all guards. The main-tree check is `.git` is a directory vs a worktree's `.git` file — NOT role-based.
coupling_points.evidence: git-shim.sh:1-14 (header), :52 (COORDINATOR var), :62-73 (is_main_tree/is_worktree via .git dir-vs-file), :146/:167/:189/:237 (per-op bypass)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: The guard discriminates main-tree-vs-worktree and a single env bypass; it has no notion of 'role'. For a solo/flat user the guard can be (a) not installed (it is only installed when `repo_config_git_attribution()` is true / via `c2c install self`), or (b) bypassed globally by exporting C2C_COORDINATOR=1. Either way the role concept is not required.

coupling_points.title: C2C_COORDINATOR gates coord-cherry-pick / coord subcommands
coupling_points.what_it_does: `c2c coord-cherry-pick` (the auto-DM-gated cherry-pick) hard-refuses unless C2C_COORDINATOR=1.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_coord.ml:202-209 (exit 1 if env != "1"); c2c_coord.ml:11 design note
coupling_points.decouple_approach: This is a structured-team workflow command; a solo/flat user never invokes it (uses plain `git cherry-pick`/merge). It is opt-in by virtue of being a separate subcommand gated on an env var, not on role metadata.

coupling_points.title: C2C_COORDINATOR allows send-as-another-alias (relay-on-behalf)
coupling_points.what_it_does: `validate_from_override` lets a caller send a DM/room message stamped with a `--from <other-alias>` they don't own ONLY if C2C_COORDINATOR=1; otherwise refuses. Same check duplicated for rooms.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:105-147 (is_coordinator + validate_from_override), ocaml/cli/c2c_rooms.ml:32,61,68
coupling_points.decouple_approach: In a flat mesh each agent only ever sends as itself, so this path is never hit. The guard's default (refuse cross-identity send) is the correct flat-mesh behavior; the coordinator bypass is purely additive and env-driven, not role-driven.

coupling_points.title: C2C_COORDINATOR exempts worktree-mismatch broker warning
coupling_points.what_it_does: Broker logs WORKTREE_MISMATCH (soft warn) when a sender's registered cwd differs from its expected-cwd file; coordinators (and remote aliases) are exempt.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:1129-1134
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Soft warn only, never blocks. For a solo user there is no expected-cwd file written unless `c2c start` wrote one; exemption is env-driven not role-driven.

coupling_points.title: `role:` string field (subagent/primary/all) — rendering only
coupling_points.what_it_does: The `role` scalar (default "subagent") is emitted into rendered frontmatter for opencode/codex and prepended to the Claude system prompt body. It does NOT gate any capability; it is a label.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_role.ml:262 (default), Claude_renderer :461 prepends r.role to body, Codex/OpenCode emit `role:` line :401,:467; no branch on its value anywhere in c2c.ml/c2c_start.ml
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Purely cosmetic/prompt-shaping. Can be dropped or ignored with zero behavioral impact.

coupling_points.title: pmodel / role_class — advisory model hint with 3-way priority
coupling_points.what_it_does: Role frontmatter `pmodel:` (or class-level lookup via `role_class` against the .c2c/config.toml [pmodel] table) supplies a default provider:model. Resolution priority on launch/resume: explicit --model flag > role pmodel > saved instance config. Role pmodel is advisory: it beats a saved config but never an explicit --model, and is never persisted.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_role.ml:300-322 (resolve_pmodel chain), ocaml/c2c_start.ml:5229-5241 (resolve_model_override priority), ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:9157-9187 (render_role_for_client/resolve_role_pmodel_for_launch)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Pure model-selection convenience. Without a role, model comes from --model or saved config. No mesh feature depends on it.

coupling_points.title: required_capabilities — pre-launch compatibility gate
coupling_points.what_it_does: If a role declares `required_capabilities` and the chosen client/binary lacks them (probed), `c2c start` exits 1 before launching. Also `compatible_clients` refuses an incompatible client.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_start.ml:3985-3988 (missing_role_capabilities), ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:9462-9481 and :9544-9563 (exit 1 on missing/incompatible)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Only fires when a role file sets these fields. No role → no gate. Flat-mesh safe by omission.

coupling_points.title: role_class → auto-join role room (coders→coders room etc.)
coupling_points.what_it_does: When C2C_AUTO_JOIN_ROLE_ROOM=1 and a role_class is set, build_env appends a `<role_class>s` room to the auto-join list (e.g. coder→coders). Install writes C2C_AUTO_JOIN_ROLE_ROOM=1.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_start.ml:2905-2924 (build_env role_class_opt branch), ocaml/c2c_role.ml:564-567 (role_class_to_room), ocaml/cli/c2c_setup.ml:509 (writes the env flag); NOTE role_class_opt defaults None and cmd_start does not pass it
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Structured-team nicety. Note the wiring appears partially dormant (build_env's role_class_opt arg is not threaded from cmd_start, defaulting None). Flat mesh just uses swarm-lounge. Removable.

coupling_points.title: Tier command-hiding is role-AGNOSTIC (keys on session-id env, not role)
coupling_points.what_it_does: Tier 3/4 commands are hidden when `is_agent_session()` is true; that predicate is solely `C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID` present. No role/coordinator concept involved.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_commands.ml:112-135 (is_agent_session = session_id_from_env present; tier_visible/filter_commands), ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:371,12144-12155 (dev-group tier filter)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already role-agnostic — it separates 'managed agent' from 'human operator' by env, which is orthogonal to role/coordinator. Keep as-is.

coupling_points.title: Broker registration `role` field — optional display metadata
coupling_points.what_it_does: Registration carries an optional `role : string option`, surfaced in `c2c list`. It is never required and gates nothing; `register` works with role=None.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_mcp.ml:208-214 (role emitted only when Some), :1883/:1970-1972 (role optional, preserved-or-None on re-register), :289 (str_opt)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already optional. Solo user registers with no role and everything works.

coupling_points.title: `coordinator1` hardcoded as default permission supervisor / authorizer fallback
coupling_points.what_it_does: The kimi PreToolUse approval hook and the opencode plugin both default the permission-approval recipient to alias `coordinator1` when no authorizers/supervisors are configured. `c2c doctor` shows 'coordinator1 (default)'.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_kimi_hook.ml:230 (AUTHORIZERS+=("coordinator1")), data/opencode-plugin/c2c.ts:102 (return ["coordinator1"]) + embedded ocaml/cli/c2c_opencode_plugin_embedded.ml:16, ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:1952/1959/10840 (doctor text)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Override via authorizers[]/supervisors[] in .c2c/repo.json or C2C_PERMISSION_SUPERVISOR/C2C_SUPERVISORS env. For a solo user with no second agent, permission-forwarding is moot (the feature only matters for client-gated approval flows). The hardcoded default could be made 'no supervisor → approve locally / no-op' so a flat solo mesh needs zero coordinator concept. Authorizers module itself does NOT hardcode coordinator1 (c2c_authorizers.ml reads repo.json only) — the hardcode lives in the two hook/plugin shells.

coupling_points.title: `swarm-lounge` hardcoded as default auto-join room
coupling_points.what_it_does: `c2c install` and start defaults write C2C_MCP_AUTO_JOIN_ROOMS="swarm-lounge"; many code paths default the room to swarm-lounge.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_setup.ml:508,579,697,805,1161,1457; ocaml/c2c_start.ml:2826,5573; ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:6940 (init --room default)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: `c2c init --room <name>` or `--room ''` (empty to skip) already overrides. A solo user can skip rooms entirely; the broker has no required-room concept. Removable default.

coupling_points.title: Reserved/protected alias list includes coordinator1 + named coders
coupling_points.what_it_does: `instances clean-stale` protects a hardcoded list of swarm aliases (coordinator1, stanza-coder, …) from being swept. Also a `--with-named-aliases` flag references them.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:7708-7719 (clean_stale_protected_aliases), :7808 (flag doc)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Tier-3 maintenance command, off by default for these aliases; purely a safety list of well-known names. Irrelevant to a solo user; can be emptied or made config-driven.

coupling_points.title: Built-in role templates (coder/coordinator/subagent) + role-designer
coupling_points.what_it_does: `c2c agent new` and prompt_for_role expand a matching role_class into a full template body (coder/coordinator/subagent) baked into the binary; role-designer is an embedded role for authoring new roles.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/role_templates.ml:8-403 (3 templates + render), ocaml/cli/c2c_agent.ml:283-285 (render on agent new), ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:9082 (prompt_for_role), ocaml/cli/role_designer_embedded.ml:1-50
coupling_points.decouple_approach: These are authoring conveniences invoked only when a user explicitly creates a structured role. They are inert for a flat/solo mesh. The 'coordinator' template embeds swarm/peer-PASS norms but produces only text + the coordinator:true field.

coupling_points.title: Role-derived heartbeat/schedule persistence
coupling_points.what_it_does: A role's c2c.heartbeat/c2c.heartbeats frontmatter is converted to managed_heartbeat specs and persisted to .c2c/schedules/<alias>/ at start; the schedule watcher picks them up. Role can also filter heartbeats by role_class.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_start.ml:891-1063 (role heartbeat merge), :1133-1143 (persist), :939-949 (should_heartbeat_apply_to_role)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Without a role the builtin default heartbeat still applies (builtin_managed_heartbeat, c2c_start.ml:180-192); role only customizes it. role_classes filter defaults to [] = apply-to-all. Flat-mesh safe.

irreducible_core: The broker/mesh layer is already fully role-agnostic: register/send/list/rooms/poll_inbox require no role; registration `role` is optional display metadata (ocaml/c2c_mcp.ml:208-214). This is the universal flat-peer core and should stay.
Tier command-hiding keyed on C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID presence (ocaml/cli/c2c_commands.ml:113-120) — a managed-vs-human distinction orthogonal to roles. Keep.
`c2c start <client>` with no `--agent` and no name-matching role file already launches a flat full-capability peer (ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:9633-9655). The opt-in mechanism exists.

The destructive-git-op guard discriminates main-tree (`.git` dir) vs worktree (`.git` file) and a single env bypass (git-shim.sh:62-73) — no role concept. The safe default (refuse main-tree mutation) is correct for any single-tree user; bypass is env-driven.
The default heartbeat (builtin_managed_heartbeat) applies with no role; role only customizes cadence/message (ocaml/c2c_start.ml:180-192).
simplification_opportunities: Decouple the capability bypass from the word 'coordinator': C2C_COORDINATOR=1 is already the real gate and is independently env-settable, so the `coordinator: true` role field (c2c_start.ml:4396-4402) is the only role→capability link. Rename/reframe it as an explicit per-session privilege flag (e.g. `C2C_ALLOW_MAINTREE_OPS`) decoupled from team structure, making the role field a pure convenience that never needs to exist for a solo user.

Make the hardcoded `coordinator1` permission-supervisor default (c2c_kimi_hook.ml:230, c2c.ts:102) resolve to a no-op / approve-locally when no authorizers and no second peer exist, so a solo/flat mesh needs zero coordinator alias. The authorizers OCaml module (c2c_authorizers.ml) is already clean — only the two shell/TS hooks hardcode the name.

Make `swarm-lounge` auto-join an explicit opt-in (or default-empty) in `c2c install`/`c2c init` (c2c_setup.ml:508 et al.) so a solo user is not auto-joined to a social room they don't need; `--room ''` already supports skipping.

Drop or stop emitting the cosmetic `role:` scalar (subagent/primary/all) — it gates nothing (only Claude/Codex/OpenCode renderer prefixing), reducing the surface that looks like a capability when it isn't.

Treat 'structured team' as a layered profile: a single `c2c init --team` (or repo.json flag) that turns on authorizers/coordinator-bypass/role-rooms/named-aliases as a bundle, leaving the default install as flat-mesh-only. Today these are scattered defaults (swarm-lounge, coordinator1, C2C_AUTO_JOIN_ROLE_ROOM=1) that an operator must individually unset to get a clean flat mesh.

The build_env `role_class_opt` parameter (c2c_start.ml:2905) appears dormant — not threaded from cmd_start — so role-room auto-join may already be partly inert; verify and either wire or remove to cut dead role-coupling.
open_questions: Is build_env's `role_class_opt` (c2c_start.ml:2905-2924) ever passed a Some value? cmd_start's build_env call (c2c_start.ml:4381-4384) does not appear to thread it, so the role_class→role-room auto-join may be effectively dead code despite C2C_AUTO_JOIN_ROLE_ROOM=1 being written by install. Worth confirming who, if anyone, sets it.

Beyond the kimi hook and opencode plugin, does the claude permission flow have a hardcoded coordinator1 default? The opencode/kimi paths were confirmed; the claude-side approval-forwarding default was not located in this pass.

What is the desired solo-user behavior for client permission-gating with no supervisor configured — approve locally (no-op) or fail-closed? Currently kimi falls closed / DMs coordinator1 (c2c_kimi_hook.ml:230-237) which would dead-letter in a solo mesh with no coordinator1 alive.

Does any relay/federation path stamp or require a role/coordinator identity remotely? The broker design is local-only today; confirm no relay-side role assumption before declaring the mesh fully flat-capable for the remote-transport future.

dimension: Tier system / agent-session command visibility filtering
summary: The tier system is a single-axis UX declutter, NOT a security boundary, and NOT role-derived. The only runtime input is whether `C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID` is present in the environment (`is_agent_session()` at c2c_commands.ml:113-114). There is no role-file read, no coordinator-flag read, no managed-ness check, and no config lookup anywhere in the tier logic — all 5 call sites (c2c.ml:371, 11799, 12154, 12315, 12323; c2c_commands.ml:117-135) consult only that one env var. When present, Tier3/Tier4 commands are dropped from the cmdliner command group, so they become "unknown command" (verified: `setcap` rejected under `C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID=fake`). But the gate is trivially bypassed by `env -u C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID c2c setcap ...` (verified — setcap man page renders), so it cannot stop an adversarial agent; it only prevents accidental invocation and shrinks the help surface. `C2C_COORDINATOR=1` does NOT affect tiers at all (verified: setcap still hidden with it set) — it is an orthogonal mechanism used by `c2c coord` and the git shim. The real destructive-op safety boundary is `c2c_git_shim.ml` + the `C2C_COORDINATOR` env check inside command bodies (e.g. c2c_coord.ml:202-209), entirely separate from tiers. The whole ladder collapses cleanly to a single "show advanced" preference / flag.

coupling_points.title: Tier gate keyed solely on C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID presence (is_agent_session)
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_commands.ml:113-114 (let is_agent_session () = match C2c_mcp.session_id_from_env () with Some _ -> true | None -> false); session_id_from_env at ocaml/c2c_mcp_helpers_post_broker.ml:705-721 reads C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID
coupling_points.what_it_does: Single boolean 'am I inside an agent session' derived only from whether the broker session-id env var is set. Drives every tier-visibility decision. No role, no coordinator flag, no config, no managed-ness consulted.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Rename the predicate to a preference, e.g. read C2C_HIDE_ADVANCED (default on when a session-id is present, overridable). Keeps the accidental-footgun protection without any role/coordinator concept. Solo user with no managed session sees everything by default.

coupling_points.title: tier_visible / filter_commands: Tier3+Tier4 hidden in agent sessions
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_commands.ml:117-135 (tier_visible: Tier1|Tier2->true, Tier3|Tier4->not(is_agent_session())); applied at c2c.ml:12323 (visible_cmds = filter_commands ~cmds:all_cmds) feeding Cmdliner.Cmd.group at c2c.ml:12326
coupling_points.what_it_does: Removes Tier3/Tier4 commands from the cmdliner group when in an agent session. Because they are absent from the group, they are non-dispatchable ('unknown command'), not merely hidden from help. Verified: setcap rejected under C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID=fake; reappears under env -u.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: This is the whole ladder. Collapse Tier1/Tier2 into 'always shown' and Tier3/Tier4 into 'advanced, shown when C2C_HIDE_ADVANCED unset or --all passed'. A two-state visible/advanced split fully replaces the four-tier type with zero behavior loss.

coupling_points.title: command_tier_map: static name->tier table (the enforcement source of truth)
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_commands.ml:20-110. Tier3: setcap (c2c_commands.ml:83). Tier4: serve, mcp, state-read, state-write, supervisor, supervisor-*, room-invite (c2c_commands.ml:96-109). Everything else Tier1/Tier2; unknown names default Tier2 (c2c_commands.ml:129).
coupling_points.what_it_does: Maps each top-level command name to a tier. The ACTUAL set blocked from agents at top level is small: setcap (Tier3) + serve, mcp, supervisor (Tier4). Verified via unknown-command listing diff: only setcap/mcp/serve/supervisor differ between agent and non-agent dispatch.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Replace the 4-value tier column with a boolean 'advanced'. Only ~4 top-level entries actually need 'advanced=true' (setcap, serve, mcp, supervisor); the rest become the default-visible core. Newly-added commands already default to visible (Tier2), so a boolean default-false 'advanced' preserves the anti-regression property.

coupling_points.title: dev group internal tier filtering (separate from filter_commands)
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:12147-12157: tier2_subs = [instances, worktree, sitrep, peer-pass] always; tier3_subs = [diag, restart_self, smoke_test, inject] only when not is_agent_session(). Verified: agent 'c2c dev' shows only peer-pass/sitrep/worktree(+instances); non-agent adds diag/restart-self/smoke-test/inject.
coupling_points.what_it_does: A second, hand-rolled copy of the agent-session check inside the dev subgroup, hiding diag/restart-self/smoke-test/inject from agents. Not driven by command_tier_map — it's an inline if on is_agent_session().
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Fold into the same 'advanced' predicate. restart-self has a genuine footgun rationale (kills supervisor inside managed session, per c2c.ml:11706-11708) but that is still session-shaped, not role-shaped; an 'advanced'/confirmation gate covers it.

coupling_points.title: commands_by_safety audit display DIVERGES from enforcement map
coupling_points.evidence: Audit display tier3 list at c2c.ml:332-352 classifies install/relay/setcap/inject/smoke-test/diag/gui/init/hook as Tier3 ('UNSAFE FOR AGENTS'). But command_tier_map enforces install=Tier2 (c2c_commands.ml:84), gui=Tier1 (:85), diag=Tier1 (:86), inject=Tier1 (:89), smoke-test=Tier1 (:88), relay=Tier2 (:79), hook=Tier1 (:95). Verified: install/relay/gui ARE visible to agents despite the audit calling them Tier3.
coupling_points.what_it_does: The human-facing `c2c commands` audit and the `commands_man` help prose label commands with tiers that do not match what filter_commands actually enforces. The audit is a hand-maintained second list that has drifted.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Delete the duplicate hand-maintained tier lists in commands_by_safety_cmd (c2c.ml:279-372), fast_path_commands (c2c.ml:11791+), and commands_man (c2c.ml:11668-11718); generate all display from the single command_tier_map. Collapsing to a boolean 'advanced' removes the drift surface entirely.

coupling_points.title: C2C_COORDINATOR=1 is ORTHOGONAL to tiers (not a tier input)
coupling_points.evidence: is_coordinator at c2c.ml:105-106 (C2C_COORDINATOR=Some"1"); used by validate_from_override (c2c.ml:108-147) and run_coord_cherry_pick (c2c_coord.ml:202-209). NOT referenced anywhere in c2c_commands.ml tier logic. Verified: C2C_COORDINATOR=1 + agent session still hides setcap (count 0).
coupling_points.what_it_does: Coordinator privilege (send-as-other-alias, coord cherry-pick, git-shim bypass) is a wholly separate env-gated mechanism. Tier visibility never consults it. The coord command group is itself NOT in the tier map, so it defaults Tier2 (visible to agents in help) but its bodies hard-fail without C2C_COORDINATOR=1.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: For the flat-mesh goal, coordinator-gated commands (coord cherry-pick, send-as-other) can become opt-in team features behind the same C2C_COORDINATOR flag, untouched by tier collapse. No role file is involved — it is a single env flag, already role-agnostic in mechanism.

coupling_points.title: Real destructive-op safety boundary is the git shim, not tiers
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_git_shim.ml exists as a separate guard; CLAUDE.md documents it refuses reset/commit/switch/checkout/rebase in the main tree for non-coordinator agents with C2C_COORDINATOR=1 bypass. Tier logic (c2c_commands.ml) never touches git ops.
coupling_points.what_it_does: The actual protection against agents doing destructive git ops is the installed git wrapper shim + C2C_COORDINATOR bypass, completely independent of the command-tier filter. This confirms tiers are UX, not the security layer.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Irrelevant to tier collapse — leave the git shim as the (separately opt-in) team-safety feature. Documenting that tiers are NOT a security boundary prevents future code from mistakenly relying on them for safety.

irreducible_core: The messaging/query/lifecycle commands (Tier1+Tier2: send, list, whoami, poll-inbox, peek-inbox, send-all, rooms, history, status, register, start, stop, restart, init, install, config, schedule, etc.) are already fully role-agnostic and unconditionally visible — this IS the universal core a solo/flat-mesh user needs.
The mechanism is role-free today: the only runtime input is C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID presence. No code reads a role file, coordinator alias, or team config to decide tier visibility.

'Hide a handful of internal-plumbing and footgun commands by default in a managed session' is a reasonable universal default that survives in a flat-mesh world as a simple preference (setcap needs sudo anyway; serve/mcp/supervisor are subprocess-internal; restart-self kills your own supervisor).
Newly-added commands default to visible-with-care (Tier2, c2c_commands.ml:129) — a good safe default that a boolean 'advanced=false' preserves.
simplification_opportunities: Collapse the 4-value `safety` type (c2c_types.ml:8-12) to a 2-state visible/advanced (or just a boolean `advanced` column on the command map). At the top level only setcap, serve, mcp, supervisor are actually agent-blocked; Tier1 vs Tier2 has zero behavioral difference today (both always visible) — the distinction is purely cosmetic labeling in help.

Replace `is_agent_session()` as the tier gate with a `C2C_HIDE_ADVANCED` preference (default: on when a session-id is present, off otherwise; overridable by flag/env). This is the 'single show-advanced flag' the north star asks for — solo user defaults to a clean surface but can opt into everything with one env var or `--all`, zero role concept.

Eliminate the THREE drifted hand-maintained tier lists: command_tier_map (enforcement, c2c_commands.ml:20-110), commands_by_safety_cmd display (c2c.ml:284-363), and commands_man help prose (c2c.ml:11668-11718) plus fast_path_commands (c2c.ml:11791+). Generate all display from the single map. The audit display already lies (calls install/relay/gui 'Tier3 UNSAFE' while enforcement makes them visible).
Delete the dev-group inline tier check (c2c.ml:12147-12157) duplication and route it through the same advanced predicate as filter_commands.

Document in code+CLAUDE.md that tiers are NOT a security boundary (the env gate is bypassable with `env -u C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID`); the real safety layer is the git shim + C2C_COORDINATOR. Prevents future code from mistakenly hanging enforcement on tiers.

Keep coordinator/team features (coord group, send-as-other, git shim) behind the existing C2C_COORDINATOR env flag as opt-in — they are already role-file-free and orthogonal to the tier collapse, so a flat-mesh build can simply never set that flag.
open_questions: restart-self under `c2c dev` has a genuine footgun (signals inner client, kills supervisor inside a managed session — c2c.ml:11706-11708). Should it stay 'advanced-hidden' for managed sessions specifically, or move to a confirmation prompt? It is session-shaped not role-shaped, so either way no role concept is needed.

The audit-display drift (install/relay/gui labeled Tier3 'UNSAFE' but enforced as visible) — is the audit aspirational (intent: these SHOULD be hidden) or stale (intent: enforcement is correct, audit wrong)? Determines whether the fix tightens enforcement or fixes the labels. Given agents routinely run `c2c install`, enforcement (visible) is almost certainly the intended behavior and the audit labels are stale.

Does anything outside the CLI (docs, scripts, role templates) parse `c2c commands` audit output and depend on the four-tier labels? A grep of scripts/ + .collab/ would confirm the audit can be safely collapsed without breaking tooling.

dimension: Approval / supervisor / reviewer-gate machinery (who can approve a tool-use)
summary: The "who can approve" decision is NOT inherently hierarchical: the single enforced authority check across both the broker (ocaml/c2c_pending_reply_handlers.ml:156) and the CLI (ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:6288-6298) is flat list membership — `List.mem reply_from_alias pending.supervisors`. There is no role lookup, no supervisor-over-subordinate relation, and no special-casing of `coordinator1` anywhere in the broker/approval code (grep found zero). The supervisors list is chosen by the REQUESTER at open-pending-reply time and can contain any alias — including the requester's own, so symmetric peer-approval and self-approval are already mechanically supported at the broker layer (only the opencode plugin actively self-excludes). The coupling to coordinator/roles is entirely SOFT: `coordinator1` is a hardcoded default STRING (fallback) in three places, and the role-file `coordinator: true` field only sets `C2C_COORDINATOR=1` which gates unrelated relay/git ops, never approval authority. The entire approval surface is also DEFAULT-OFF on every client (kimi block ships commented out, Claude hook ships with a never-matching sentinel matcher, opencode only fires when opencode itself is set to "ask"), so a solo user is never gated unless they opt in. However, there IS a real solo-user footgun once opted in: in the opencode plugin a lone self-as-supervisor collapses to an empty supervisor set yet still runs the wait loop → guaranteed 10-min timeout → fail-closed auto-reject; the kimi hook falls back to a possibly-nonexistent `coordinator1` and also falls closed.

coupling_points.title: Authority check is flat list-membership, not hierarchy
coupling_points.what_it_does: The broker's check_pending_reply and the CLI's do_approval_reply both authorize a verdict by testing whether the replying alias is in pending.supervisors. No role, tier, or seniority is consulted; any alias the requester listed is equally authoritative.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_pending_reply_handlers.ml:156 `if List.mem reply_from_alias pending.supervisors`; ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:6288-6298 `if not (List.exists (fun s -> alias_casefold s = alias_casefold reviewer_alias) pending.supervisors) then ... exit 1`
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already role-agnostic — this is the irreducible core. Keep as-is. For a flat mesh, the requester simply lists peer aliases (or its own alias for self-approval). No code change needed to support symmetric peer-approval.

coupling_points.title: `coordinator1` hardcoded as the last-resort supervisor default
coupling_points.what_it_does: When no authorizers/supervisors are configured anywhere, the kimi hook, the opencode plugin, and the repo.json examples all fall back to the literal alias `coordinator1`. This is the only place the approval path 'knows' about a coordinator, and it is a plain string default, not a privileged identity.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_kimi_hook.ml:230 `AUTHORIZERS+=("coordinator1")`; ocaml/cli/c2c_opencode_plugin_embedded.ml:105 `return ["coordinator1"]`; .c2c/repo.json supervisors=["coordinator1"]; broker grep shows NO special-casing of the name
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Replace the `coordinator1` literal default with: (a) for solo, default to the agent's OWN alias (self-approve) or to OFF; (b) for mesh, no default at all → if supervisors empty, treat as 'no gate' rather than 'ask coordinator1'. Make the default configurable via repo.json `default_supervisor` or just drop it.

coupling_points.title: Solo-user fail-closed when supervisor set collapses to empty (opencode)
coupling_points.what_it_does: selectSupervisors() filters out the agent's own alias; if the agent is the only configured supervisor the result is []. The flow still proceeds into waitForPermissionReply with no DM recipients, so it can never get a reply → after C2C_PERMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS (default 600000ms / 10min) it auto-rejects (fail-closed). A solo user who turned permission-ask on is blocked 10 minutes then denied.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_opencode_plugin_embedded.ml:341-344 self-exclude → return []; line 1959 `waitForPermissionReply(permId, permissionTimeoutMs, supervisors)` runs regardless; line 1962-1964 timeout maps to `reject` (fail-closed)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Add an early escape: if selectSupervisors() returns [] then resolve the permission as ALLOW (or surface a local prompt) instead of entering the wait loop. Solo = no remote supervisor = either auto-allow or local-only gate. Also lets self-approval through (don't self-exclude when the list is exactly [self]).

coupling_points.title: Kimi hook falls back to coordinator1 then fails closed if absent
coupling_points.what_it_does: resolve_authorizers reads repo.json authorizers[]; if absent uses C2C_KIMI_APPROVAL_REVIEWER (deprecated) else literal coordinator1. It then DMs that alias and blocks on await-reply; if the alias does not exist / never replies, every tier times out and the hook exits 2 (deny). A solo user with no coordinator1 peer is hard-denied.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_kimi_hook.ml:169-237 (resolve + fallback to coordinator1); lines 322-345 send + await-reply + `exit 2` on empty verdict; the script falls closed by design
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Same as opencode: if no real authorizer resolves (none alive), and in solo mode, fail-OPEN or route to self via the local `c2c authorize` CLI. The is_safe_command allowlist (lines 115-156) already lets read-only commands through without any supervisor — extend that posture so absence-of-supervisor != hard deny.

coupling_points.title: supervisor_strategy (first-alive | round-robin | broadcast) routing
coupling_points.what_it_does: repo.json supervisor_strategy selects how the configured supervisor list is fanned out. Implemented in the opencode plugin (c2c_opencode_plugin_embedded.ml:346-359) and stubbed in the kimi hook (only first-alive implemented; round-robin/broadcast fall back to first-alive). Pure routing over a flat list — does not change WHO is authoritative, only the order/breadth of who is asked.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_kimi_hook.ml:186-208,299-399 (strategy resolver + dispatcher, round-robin/broadcast not implemented); ocaml/cli/c2c_opencode_plugin_embedded.ml:290-359
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already role-agnostic (operates over alias list). Trivially works for a 2-peer mesh. Can stay as opt-in; for solo it is moot (list of 0/1).

coupling_points.title: coord_fallthrough broker scheduler (per-DM redundancy chain)
coupling_points.what_it_does: A 60s broker thread escalates unanswered permission DMs down `[swarm] coord_chain` aliases, then broadcasts to swarm-lounge. Reads verbatim aliases from .c2c/config.toml coord_chain; DEFAULT is [] (feature OFF). Skips offline aliases, stamps fired tiers, stops when check_pending_reply marks resolved_at.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/coord_fallthrough.ml:89-150 (decide_next_action over chain); ocaml/c2c_start.ml:745-753 `swarm_config_coord_chain` defaults to []; broadcast room defaults swarm-lounge
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already opt-in (empty chain = disabled). It is purely an alias-chain escalator with no role semantics; the name 'coord' is cosmetic. For a flat mesh rename to e.g. `escalation_chain` and it works unchanged. Solo: leave empty (default) → no effect.

coupling_points.title: Requester binds supervisors at open_pending_reply; broker derives reply identity from session
coupling_points.what_it_does: open_pending_reply stores supervisors exactly as passed by the requester (no validation that they are 'real' coordinators) and requires the caller be a registered session. check_pending_reply derives reply_from_alias from the caller's OWN registration, not from arguments — so authority is session-bound, preventing spoofing, and is symmetric: any registered peer the requester trusts can be a supervisor.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_pending_reply_handlers.ml:14-26 (supervisors taken from arguments), :35-39 (caller must be registered), :117-123 (reply_from_alias from registration, legacy arg ignored)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: This is the clean symmetric primitive. For self-approval the requester lists its own alias; for peer-approval it lists a peer. No coordinator concept required. Keep.

coupling_points.title: Default-OFF install posture (every client)
coupling_points.what_it_does: Approval forwarding is never active out-of-the-box: kimi TOML block is shipped fully commented; Claude PreToolUse hook is installed with a sentinel matcher `__C2C_PREAUTH_DISABLED__` that matches nothing; opencode only forwards when opencode's own config sets a permission to 'ask'. So a solo user is NOT blocked waiting for a nonexistent supervisor unless they explicitly opt in.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_kimi_hook.ml:414-476 (block commented, header 'ships fully commented out'); ocaml/cli/c2c_setup.ml:1380-1397 (sentinel_matcher `__C2C_PREAUTH_DISABLED__`); c2c_opencode_plugin_embedded.ml:1903-1909 (fires only on opencode 'ask' events)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Good baseline for solo. Keep default-off; the decouple work is purely about making the opted-in path degrade gracefully (fail-open / self-approve) when no peer supervisor exists, rather than fail-closed to coordinator1.

irreducible_core: Session-bound reply identity: check_pending_reply derives the replier alias from the caller's own broker registration, not from request args (anti-spoofing) — ocaml/c2c_pending_reply_handlers.ml:117-123
Flat supervisor-list membership as the sole authority test (no roles/tiers) — c2c_pending_reply_handlers.ml:156, c2c.ml:6288-6298
File-based pending/verdict side-channel (token, atomic write, sanitized filenames) decoupled from any role concept — ocaml/cli/c2c_approval_paths.ml
Per-token TTL + capacity caps + decision audit log (pending_open/check) — independent of who the supervisors are
Default-OFF install posture across all clients (solo user is never gated unless they opt in)
is_safe_command read-only allowlist that bypasses approval entirely without any supervisor — c2c_kimi_hook.ml:115-156
simplification_opportunities: Make the empty-supervisor case fail-OPEN (or self-approve) instead of fail-closed: opencode early-returns ALLOW when selectSupervisors()=[] (c2c_opencode_plugin_embedded.ml:1940-1964) and the kimi hook treats 'no resolvable authorizer' as allow-in-solo rather than exit 2 (c2c_kimi_hook.ml:234-237,343). This directly fixes the solo footgun.

Drop the hardcoded `coordinator1` literal default in three places (c2c_kimi_hook.ml:230, c2c_opencode_plugin_embedded.ml:105) and replace with: solo → own alias / OFF; mesh → no default (empty = no gate). Removes the only coordinator coupling in the approval path.

Allow self-approval cleanly: stop self-excluding in opencode selectSupervisors when the list is exactly [self] (line 341); the broker already permits requester==supervisor, so a solo agent could approve its own tool-uses (or this whole path is just OFF for solo).

Collapse the two divergent kimi hook copies: the on-disk scripts/c2c-kimi-approval-hook.sh still uses the legacy single-REVIEWER model while the embedded c2c_kimi_hook.ml uses authorizers[]+strategy. The 'rough sync' convention is drift waiting to happen; embedded copy should be sole source, script regenerated from it.
Finish or delete the round-robin/broadcast strategy stubs in the kimi hook (c2c_kimi_hook.ml:357-397) — currently they just re-run first-alive, so the config value is misleading.

Rename role-flavored config keys (coord_chain, coord_fallthrough_*, primary_authorizer) to neutral names (escalation_chain, escalation_*) so a flat mesh reads naturally; behavior is already role-agnostic.
open_questions: Intended solo posture when opted-in but no peer exists: fail-open (allow), self-approve (own alias in supervisors), or local interactive prompt? Code currently fail-closes — is that the desired default for a flat-mesh/solo world?

Should the broker actively REJECT a supervisors list that equals [requester] (block self-approval) or explicitly bless it? Today it silently permits self-approval (no guard); the opencode plugin alone blocks it via self-exclusion — these two layers disagree.

Is there any intended privilege difference between a 'supervisor' and a peer, or is 'supervisor' purely the label for 'whoever the requester chose to gate on'? Code shows the latter; docs/role-files imply the former.

Cross-host approval is explicitly deferred (c2c_approval_paths.ml:14 'v1 is local-only') — does the flat-mesh north star require remote approval, which would change the broker_root-embedded-in-pending design?

dimension: Native scheduling / wake and its coupling to team/coordinator structure
summary: The scheduling *engine* is almost entirely role-agnostic. The schedule TOML format, the file watcher in `c2c start`, the MCP handlers, the CLI (`c2c schedule set/list/rm/...`), the fire/idle-gating helpers, and `c2c doctor schedule` carry zero coordinator/sitrep/role logic — they operate on per-alias `.c2c/schedules/<alias>/*.toml` files and idle-gate against the broker's `last_activity_ts`. `c2c install` writes exactly one universal `wake.toml` (interval 4.1m, idle-gated, message "wake — poll inbox, advance work" — no coordinator reference) for every client, which is the correct universal default for both solo and flat-mesh. The team-structure coupling lives entirely OUTSIDE the engine: (1) the *sitrep* schedule is never installed by code — it is prose in the coordinator role template instructing the agent to self-run `c2c schedule set sitrep ...`; (2) coordinator failover is a pure runbook convention with no detection or scheduling code (the `c2c failover-status` doctor check is an unchecked TODO); (3) the only code-level role hook in scheduling is `should_heartbeat_apply_to_role`, which filters on a `role_classes` field that installed/CLI-created schedules always leave empty (role-agnostic) — only role-file `c2c.heartbeats.*` YAML could inject role-gated timers, and no shipped role does. Remaining couplings are soft string defaults: the builtin heartbeat *content* hardcodes "coordinator1 (or swarm-lounge)", `swarm-lounge` is hardcoded as the default room, and the planned `swarm_config_coordinator_alias`/`social_room` thunks are comment-only stubs. A separate broker scheduler, `coord_fallthrough`, escalates unacked permission DMs through a `coord_chain` but defaults to `[]` (feature-off), so it is already opt-in.
irreducible_core: The schedule data model + persistence: per-alias `.c2c/schedules/<alias>/*.toml` with interval, align, message, only_when_idle, idle_threshold, enabled. Role-free (ocaml/cli/c2c_schedule.ml:60-73, ocaml/c2c_schedule_handlers.ml:22-35).

The idle-gating + fire logic in c2c_schedule_fire.ml: `agent_is_idle`, `last_activity_ts_for_alias`, `enqueue_heartbeat`, `should_fire` — all keyed on alias + broker last_activity_ts, no role concept (ocaml/c2c_schedule_fire.ml:6-37).

The hot-reload watcher thread in c2c_start.ml that stat-polls the schedule dir every 10s and starts/stops timers per file — role filter is a no-op when role_classes=[] which is the install/CLI default (ocaml/c2c_start.ml:1149-1221).
The universal `wake` default itself: poll inbox / advance work, 4.1m interval, idle-gated. This is the right default for a solo user and a flat mesh alike (ocaml/cli/c2c_setup.ml:1564-1576).

CLI + MCP surfaces `schedule set/list/show/rm/enable/disable` and `c2c doctor schedule` — fully role-agnostic, operate on current alias (ocaml/cli/c2c_schedule.ml:363-391, ocaml/cli/c2c_doctor_schedule.ml:48-82).
simplification_opportunities: Make the wake-default message provider-neutral: `c2c_setup.ml:1570` already uses the clean 'wake — poll inbox, advance work' (no coordinator), but the *builtin* heartbeat content in c2c_start.ml:163/172 still hardcodes 'ask coordinator1 (or swarm-lounge) for more'. In solo/flat-mesh mode that line is misleading. Replace with role/topology-neutral text, or gate the 'ask coordinator1' tail behind a swarm-mode flag.

The sitrep schedule has NO code path — it's manual prose in the coordinator role template. For a flat mesh / solo user there is nothing to remove from the engine; it simply never gets created. Keep it as a coordinator-role opt-in (already is). No engine change needed.
Coordinator failover is 100% runbook convention with zero code. For a solo/flat deployment it's a no-op already. Nothing to strip from the binary; just ensure docs don't imply the binary enforces it.
