Implement (or delete) the planned `swarm_config_coordinator_alias` / `swarm_config_social_room` thunks (c2c_start.ml:661 comment, c2c_start.mli:340). Today 'swarm-lounge' and 'coordinator1' are hardcoded in ~6 sites. A solo user has no swarm-lounge; making these config-driven with empty/disabled defaults removes the swarm assumption from the wake content and auto-join behavior.

`role_classes` on schedule entries is dead weight for the universal path (always [] from install + CLI + MCP). Could keep it as an undocumented advanced field but it adds a role concept to the schedule model that 99% of users never touch — candidate to drop from the schedule_entry surface and keep role-gating purely in the role->heartbeat layer.

`coord_fallthrough` scheduler is already opt-in (coord_chain defaults to []). For solo/flat-mesh it self-disables. Keep as opt-in structured-team feature; no change needed beyond ensuring it stays default-off.

coupling_points.title: Universal wake.toml auto-created on every install
coupling_points.what_it_does: After any `c2c install <client>` for a known client, writes a single `wake` schedule: interval 246s (4.1m), align empty, message 'wake — poll inbox, advance work', only_when_idle=true, idle_threshold=246s, enabled=true. Skips if wake.toml already exists.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_setup.ml:1551-1588 (ensure_default_wake_schedule); called at ocaml/cli/c2c_setup.ml:1641-1643 for known_clients only
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already role-agnostic and correct as the universal default. No coordinator reference in the message. Keep verbatim as the solo/flat-mesh default. Optionally make interval configurable, but the current default is fine.

coupling_points.title: Builtin heartbeat content hardcodes 'ask coordinator1 (or swarm-lounge)'
coupling_points.what_it_does: The default and push-aware managed-heartbeat message strings tell the agent: if out of work, ask coordinator1 or swarm-lounge. This is the content used by the codex builtin heartbeat and any role/config heartbeat that doesn't override `message`.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_start.ml:161-163 (default_managed_heartbeat_content), 169-172 (push_aware_heartbeat_content), 184 (builtin uses it)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Swap to topology-neutral text ('if out of work, idle or check your peers'), or template the coordinator/room names via the planned swarm_config_coordinator_alias/social_room thunks so they vanish in solo mode. Note the install-written wake.toml (c2c_setup.ml:1570) does NOT use this string, so a freshly-installed wake schedule is already clean; this only bites the codex builtin and role-default heartbeats.

coupling_points.title: role_classes filter on schedule firing (should_heartbeat_apply_to_role)
coupling_points.what_it_does: When the watcher loads a schedule TOML, it converts to a managed_heartbeat and filters with should_heartbeat_apply_to_role: if role_classes is non-empty, the timer only fires when the launched role's role_class is in the list. Empty role_classes = fire for everyone.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_start.ml:939-949 (filter), 1165-1166 (watcher applies it); schedule->heartbeat conversion sets role_classes=[] at ocaml/c2c_start.ml:868 (managed_heartbeat_of_schedule_entry)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: For all schedules created by `c2c install`, `c2c schedule set`, and MCP schedule_set, role_classes is ALWAYS [] — so the filter is a no-op on the universal path. The field is only populated via role-file `c2c.heartbeats.<name>.role_classes` YAML, which no shipped role uses. Can keep the filter (harmless when []) or drop role_classes from the schedule_entry model entirely and keep role-gating in the role->heartbeat resolution layer only.

coupling_points.title: Role-file heartbeats persisted into schedule dir (c2c.heartbeat / c2c.heartbeats)
coupling_points.what_it_does: On `c2c start` with a role file, role-declared heartbeats (c2c.heartbeat.* default override, c2c.heartbeats.<name>.* named) are resolved, role/client-filtered, and written as .toml into .c2c/schedules/<alias>/ for the watcher to pick up. This is the only path that can create a role-specific timer in code.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_start.ml:1002-1063 (resolve_managed_heartbeats_and_persist_role), 1133-1143 (persist_role_heartbeats_to_schedule_dir); role fields at ocaml/c2c_role.ml:21-22,43-44,271-272
coupling_points.decouple_approach: No shipped role (coordinator1.md, Cairn-Vigil.md, templates) actually declares c2c.heartbeat/c2c.heartbeats — they leave the c2c: block at alias + auto_join_rooms only (verified .c2c/roles/coordinator1.md:6-8). So in practice this path persists nothing extra today; the universal wake.toml from install is what runs. The mechanism is opt-in by role authorship. Solo/flat-mesh users with no role file (role=None) skip it entirely (c2c_start.ml:1009-1011 returns []).

coupling_points.title: Sitrep schedule is role-template prose, not code
coupling_points.what_it_does: Coordinator role templates instruct the agent to self-run `c2c schedule set sitrep --interval 1h --align @1h+7m --message 'sitrep tick'` (or a Monitor fallback). The binary never auto-creates a sitrep schedule; `c2c sitrep` is only a git-commit helper for .sitreps/ files.
coupling_points.evidence: .c2c/roles/coordinator1.md:30, .c2c/roles/builtins/Cairn-Vigil.md:40, .c2c/roles/builtins/templates/coordinator.md.tmpl:40,54-58; ocaml/cli/c2c_sitrep.ml:1-131 (commit-only, no schedule writes)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already fully decoupled at the code level — the engine has no sitrep concept. For solo/flat-mesh, no sitrep schedule is ever created because the coordinator role (and its prose) is never loaded. Keep sitrep as a coordinator-role opt-in. The `c2c sitrep commit` helper is harmless and role-agnostic (just commits a dated file).

coupling_points.title: Coordinator failover protocol (detection + takeover)
coupling_points.what_it_does: Defines lyra-quill as recovery agent, succession order, detection signals (no sitrep at :07, unread DMs, dead pid), and takeover/handback steps. Entirely a runbook; no scheduler watches for coord death and no code triggers failover.
coupling_points.evidence: .collab/runbooks/coordinator-failover.md:1-60; the proposed `c2c failover-status` doctor check is an UNCHECKED todo at .collab/runbooks/coordinator-failover.md:204; no failover/takeover scheduling code in ocaml/ (grep: only alias-reclaim 'takeover' in registration, ocaml/c2c.ml:3683)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Zero code to remove — failover is 100% social/runbook. For solo (no coordinator) or flat mesh (no single coordinator) it is simply inapplicable. Ensure docs frame it as a structured-team-only convention so a solo user isn't told the binary enforces a recovery chain.

coupling_points.title: coordinator-backup fallthrough broker scheduler (coord_chain)
coupling_points.what_it_does: A broker-side Lwt scheduler that, when a permission DM to the primary coord isn't acked within an idle window, escalates through coord_chain backups then broadcasts to swarm-lounge. A genuine scheduling feature that assumes a coordinator hierarchy.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/coord_fallthrough.mli:1-60; config thunks ocaml/c2c_start.ml:737-783; coord_chain defaults to [] = feature-off (c2c_start.ml:731,745-753)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Already opt-in: coord_chain defaults to [] which the scheduler treats as feature-off, so solo/flat-mesh deployments get nothing. Keep default-off. The broadcast tier defaults to 'swarm-lounge' but only fires if a chain is configured. This is the cleanest model for the rest of scheduling to follow: structured-team feature, default-disabled.

coupling_points.title: swarm-lounge hardcoded as default room + planned config thunks unimplemented
coupling_points.what_it_does: swarm-lounge is hardcoded as the auto-join room and broadcast room in multiple sites; the planned swarm_config_coordinator_alias / swarm_config_social_room helpers that would make coordinator alias and social room configurable are comment-only stubs.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_start.ml:1625,3128,5573 (hardcoded swarm-lounge default), 739 (broadcast room), 661 (planned thunks comment), ocaml/c2c_start.mli:340 (same comment); install writes C2C_MCP_AUTO_JOIN_ROOMS=swarm-lounge
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Implement swarm_config_coordinator_alias/social_room as real config reads (default empty/disabled), then thread them through the heartbeat content + auto-join defaults. A solo user sets nothing and gets no swarm-lounge auto-join and no 'ask coordinator1' tail. This is the single change that most reduces the team assumption baked into the wake/scheduling surface.

open_questions: Should the universal `wake` schedule even be auto-created for a solo user who isn't running a swarm? Today install always writes it. A solo user polling their own inbox on a 4.1m idle timer is arguably useful (self-DM scheduling, reminders) but the message text presumes swarm work. Decide: keep wake universal with neutral text, or gate auto-creation behind a swarm/agent mode.

Is `role_classes` on schedule_entry worth keeping at all? It is always [] on every code-created schedule and no shipped role populates it. Dropping it simplifies the schedule model and removes a role concept from the universal path, at the cost of breaking the (unused) ability to role-gate a schedule TOML directly.

Should `c2c schedule` support a non-self-DM target (e.g. a reminder to a peer or a room) for the flat-mesh case, or stay strictly self-DM (enqueue_message from_alias=alias to_alias=alias)? Currently it is self-DM only (c2c_schedule_fire.ml:23-27), which is the right minimal core but forecloses peer/room scheduled pings.

Do the planned swarm_config_coordinator_alias/social_room thunks get implemented or deleted? They have been comment-only stubs since #318/#341; leaving them as comments while 6 call sites hardcode the values is the actual source of the team assumption in wake content.

dimension: Default install/onboarding team-structure assumptions (c2c install + c2c init + c2c start)
summary: A brand-new solo user who runs `c2c install` (or `just install-all`) + `c2c init` + `c2c start` is implicitly enrolled into THIS dev swarm's framing at multiple layers. The hard core is small: nothing in the messaging path (register/send/poll) requires a role or coordinator, and DM-based 1:1 works role-agnostically. But the DEFAULTS lean swarm everywhere: every client's MCP env block is written with `C2C_MCP_AUTO_JOIN_ROOMS="swarm-lounge"` + `C2C_AUTO_JOIN_ROLE_ROOM="1"` (install-time, all 5 clients); the broker register/confirm handlers UNCONDITIONALLY announce `peer_register` into a hardcoded `swarm-lounge` room (broker core, ghost-room auto-create, not just config); the default kickoff/restart intro literally opens "You have been started as a c2c swarm agent... The swarm coordinates via c2c... You are now part of it"; the role-onboarding preamble and role templates hardcode "introduce yourself to coordinator1", peer-PASS gate, and named peers (Cairn-Vigil, stanza-coder…); `c2c install self` installs a `git-pre-reset` shim whose guard hard-codes a coordinator/non-coordinator split (refuses commit-on-master etc. unless `C2C_COORDINATOR=1`); the kimi PreToolUse approval hook falls back to `coordinator1` as authorizer (but is commented-out by default). Most of these are SOFT (defaults/text) and individually opt-out-able, but there is NO neutral/flat default — the union of defaults presumes a structured multi-agent swarm with a coordinator. A solo user wanting plain 1:1 between two of their own agents gets a working channel but also a phantom swarm-lounge room, swarm-agent intro text, an interactive "what's this agent's role?" prompt, and a git shim built around coordinator privilege.

coupling_points.title: Install writes swarm-lounge auto-join into every client's MCP env
coupling_points.what_it_does: Every `c2c install <client>` writes C2C_MCP_AUTO_JOIN_ROOMS="swarm-lounge" and C2C_AUTO_JOIN_ROLE_ROOM="1" into the client's MCP env block. The MCP server then auto-joins swarm-lounge on first registration (auto_join_rooms_impl). A solo user is placed into the swarm social room without asking.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_setup.ml:508-509 (codex), :579-580 (kimi), :697-698 (gemini), :805-807 (opencode), :1161-1162 (claude), :1457-1458 (crush); consumed in ocaml/c2c_mcp_helpers_post_broker.ml:1037-1064 (auto_join_rooms_impl)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Make the auto-join room a single sourced constant defaulting to empty (or to a neutral per-user room) and only write swarm-lounge when an operator opts into swarm mode (e.g. `c2c install --swarm` or a repo.json flag). C2C_AUTO_JOIN_ROLE_ROOM is already inert without a role file, so it can simply be dropped from the default.

coupling_points.title: Broker hardcodes swarm-lounge for the peer_register announcement (CORE, not config)
coupling_points.what_it_does: On every new registration AND on unconfirmed→confirmed promotion, the broker builds `social_rooms = sort_uniq ("swarm-lounge" :: auto_rooms)` and send_room's a `"<alias> registered"` announcement into it. swarm-lounge is prepended UNCONDITIONALLY, independent of C2C_MCP_AUTO_JOIN_ROOMS. send_room auto-creates a ghost room (members=[], created_by="") and writes room-history, so a solo broker silently materializes a swarm-lounge room on first registration.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_identity_handlers.ml:340-360 (register handler, line 349 `"swarm-lounge" :: auto_rooms`); ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:4064-4084 (confirm path, line 4073 same); send_room ghost-room behavior ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:3849-3887
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Drop the hardcoded `"swarm-lounge" ::` prefix; announce only into rooms the agent actually joined (auto_rooms), or skip the broadcast entirely when no social room is configured. Currently harmless for a true solo (no members → history-only) but it writes a phantom room and bakes the swarm assumption into broker core.

coupling_points.title: Default kickoff / restart intro frames the agent as a swarm member
coupling_points.what_it_does: builtin_swarm_restart_intro (rendered by default_kickoff_prompt on `c2c start` when --auto or a role file is present) opens 'You have been started as a c2c swarm agent...', instructs 'Post in the lounge: send_room swarm-lounge', and closes 'The swarm coordinates via c2c instant messaging. You are now part of it.' This is the first thing a managed agent reads.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_start.ml:668-678 (builtin_swarm_restart_intro); ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:9118-9150 (default_kickoff_prompt renders it); also default_managed_heartbeat_content references 'ask coordinator1 (or swarm-lounge)' at ocaml/c2c_start.ml:161-163 and 169-172
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Make the intro neutral by default ('You can message peers with c2c send / poll_inbox') and move the swarm/lounge/coordinator framing into a swarm-mode override. The override mechanism already exists ([swarm] restart_intro in .c2c/config.toml, swarm_config_restart_intro) — invert the default so swarm framing is opt-in. Same for the heartbeat content's coordinator1 reference.

coupling_points.title: Role onboarding preamble + role templates hardcode coordinator1 and named peers
coupling_points.what_it_does: When launched with --agent / a role file, the kickoff preamble tells the agent: 'Join swarm-lounge... Send a message to coordinator1 introducing yourself'. The role-class templates (Role_templates.render) embed THIS swarm's specifics: 'senior coder on the c2c swarm', peers 'coordinator1 (Cairn-Vigil), stanza-coder, galaxy-coder...', the peer-PASS gate, 'DM coordinator1 with peer-PASS by <peer>'.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:9496-9506 and 9573-9584 (onboarding_preamble, both role paths); ocaml/cli/role_templates.ml:10,21,24,35,38,42-45,80,93,100,119-120 (coder template); ocaml/cli/role_designer_embedded.ml:5,17,59,92
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Templates and the preamble are only reached via the role path (opt-in). Strip the THIS-swarm-specific named peers / coordinator1 / peer-PASS text into a separately-sourced 'team profile' so the generic role templates stay role-agnostic; or gate the coordinator-introduction step on a configured supervisor existing.

coupling_points.title: Interactive 'what is this agent's role?' prompt on plain `c2c start`
coupling_points.what_it_does: On a TTY with no role file and no explicit kickoff, `c2c start` interactively prompts: 'What is this agent's role? (e.g. coder, planner, coordinator — press Enter to skip)' and, if answered, writes a role file and expands the swarm role template. Presumes role-structured team membership; a solo 1:1 user is nudged toward picking a role.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:9069-9108 (prompt_for_role); called from the no-role start paths at c2c.ml:9604, 9621, 9644
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Default to skipping the role prompt (or make it a single y/N 'configure a structured role? [N]'); Enter already skips, but the prompt itself presumes roles are the norm. A flat-mesh default would not prompt at all.

coupling_points.title: `c2c install self` installs a coordinator-gated git pre-reset shim
coupling_points.what_it_does: `c2c install self` / `install all` unconditionally installs git + git-pre-reset shims via ensure_swarm_git_shim_installed. The guard (git-shim.sh) refuses git commit-on-master, reset --hard, switch/checkout/rebase in the main tree for anyone WITHOUT C2C_COORDINATOR=1. This encodes a two-tier coordinator/non-coordinator model into the user's git, irrelevant and obstructive to a solo user.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_setup.ml:306-313 (install self installs shim); ocaml/c2c_start.ml:1879-1906 (install_pre_reset_shim / ensure_swarm_git_shim_installed); git-shim.sh:3-4,52,62-67,107-174 (COORDINATOR gate, refuses commit on main unless C2C_COORDINATOR=1); is_coordinator reads C2C_COORDINATOR at ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:105-106
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Do NOT install the git shim as part of default `install self`. Gate it behind an explicit `c2c install git-shim` / `--swarm` opt-in (uninstall already supports git-shim as a component). For a solo user the shim has no upside (no peers to protect commits from) and actively breaks normal solo git on master.

coupling_points.title: Kimi PreToolUse approval hook falls back to coordinator1 authorizer
coupling_points.what_it_does: The kimi approval hook resolves the authorizer chain; if repo.json has no authorizers[] and no env var, it falls back to literal 'coordinator1'. If the [[hooks]] block were enabled, every non-safe kimi tool call would DM a non-existent coordinator1 and block until timeout/fall-closed. Mitigated: the [[hooks]] TOML block is installed FULLY-COMMENTED by default, so the hook is dormant unless the operator uncomments it.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_kimi_hook.ml:163-180,219-237 (resolve_authorizers + line 230 fallback coordinator1); installed commented per ocaml/cli/c2c_setup.ml:607-616 and c2c_kimi_hook.ml:12 ('fully-commented [[hooks]] block'); CLI --reviewer default 'coordinator1' at ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:6509
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Change the last-resort fallback from 'coordinator1' to fall-open (exit 0) or to a clear 'no authorizer configured — approval disabled' rather than a hardcoded swarm alias. Since the block is commented by default this is low-severity, but the hardcoded alias is the wrong default for solo.

coupling_points.title: Supervisor/authorizer display + docs default to coordinator1
coupling_points.what_it_does: `c2c doctor` and help text present coordinator1 as the implied supervisor default ('supervisor: coordinator1 (default...)', 'authorizers: ... fallback: coordinator1 implicit'). The actual resolver (C2c_authorizers / MCP permission path) returns None/[] when unconfigured — so this is display/doc text, not enforced behavior, for the claude/opencode MCP path.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:1952 (doctor supervisor default text), :1959 (authorizers fallback text), :7310-7311,10862-10863 (help examples); resolver returns None when unset: ocaml/cli/c2c_authorizers.ml:50-69; MCP permission supervisors default to [] at ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:1006-1011
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Reword doctor/help to not present a specific alias as the universal default; say 'no supervisor configured (approvals disabled)'. The code already does the right (neutral) thing; only the surfaced text presumes coordinator1.

coupling_points.title: README/c2c init onboarding centered on swarm-lounge
coupling_points.what_it_does: README 'Quick Start' frames onboarding as 'configure your client, register, join swarm-lounge', and `c2c init` has --room defaulting to swarm-lounge (joins it on init). Opt-out exists ('Pass empty string to skip'), but the documented and default happy-path puts the solo user in the swarm social room.
coupling_points.evidence: README.md:11,17; ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:6939-6942 (--room default swarm-lounge), :7056-7064 (join on init), :7299-7307 (init doc 'join swarm-lounge')
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Default `c2c init --room` to empty (skip), and document a neutral 1:1 path first ('register two agents, c2c send between them'), with 'join swarm-lounge / swarm mode' as an explicit opt-in section.

coupling_points.title: Hardcoded protected-alias list of this swarm's named agents
coupling_points.what_it_does: `instances clean-stale` protects a hardcoded list of THIS swarm's specific aliases (coordinator1, swarm-lounge, stanza-coder, jungle-coder, galaxy-coder, lyra-quill, test-agent, dogfood-hunter). Not part of solo onboarding, but it bakes this particular team's roster into the binary.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:7708-7719 (clean_stale_protected_aliases)
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Derive the protected set from live registrations / configured supervisors rather than a hardcoded roster, or make it config-driven. Only protect swarm-lounge structurally if swarm mode is on.

coupling_points.title: Default wake schedule created at install (neutral content)
coupling_points.what_it_does: `c2c install <client>` calls ensure_default_wake_schedule, writing a wake.toml (interval 4.1m, idle-gated) with message 'wake — poll inbox, advance work'. This presumes an autonomous always-on agent loop. The message itself is role-neutral (no coordinator/swarm reference), so it is the least-coupled of the defaults — but it still assumes an autonomous-agent posture rather than an on-demand 1:1 tool.
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/cli/c2c_setup.ml:1551-1588 (ensure_default_wake_schedule, message at :1570); invoked at :1642-1643
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Keep as-is for managed/autonomous use, but consider not creating a wake schedule for a non-autonomous solo install (or gate on swarm/autonomous mode). Low priority — content is already neutral.

irreducible_core: The messaging path is already role/coordinator-agnostic: register (C2C_MCP_AUTO_REGISTER_ALIAS), send/poll_inbox, list, whoami — none require a role, a supervisor, or swarm-lounge (ocaml/c2c_identity_handlers.ml, c2c_mcp_helpers_post_broker.ml).
Alias assignment is neutral: auto-generated word-pair aliases with no role/coordinator concept (ocaml/cli/c2c_setup.ml:92-113, default_alias_for_client).
Per-agent broker registration + inbox + 1:1 DM delivery is the genuine universal core and works for two of a user's own agents with zero team structure.
Rooms as a generic primitive (join_room/send_room/room_history) are role-agnostic — only the swarm-lounge DEFAULT and the broker's hardcoded prepend are coupled, not the room machinery itself.

The MCP permission/supervisor path already defaults to an empty supervisor list and the authorizers resolver returns None when unconfigured — the neutral behavior already exists in code; only defaults/text presume coordinator1.
broker-root resolution, identity/Ed25519 keys, and relay transport are all independent of team structure.
simplification_opportunities: Introduce a single explicit mode switch (e.g. `c2c install --swarm` / repo.json `"mode":"swarm"`) and make the FLAT/solo behavior the default: no swarm-lounge auto-join, neutral kickoff intro, no git-shim, no role prompt. Swarm framing becomes additive opt-in.

Source the social-room name from ONE place. Today 'swarm-lounge' is hardcoded in ~10 spots (setup_*.ml x6, c2c_start.ml multiple, c2c_identity_handlers.ml:349, c2c_broker.ml:4073, c2c.ml init/help). A single `swarm_config_social_room ()` thunk (already planned per the #318 comment at c2c_start.ml:660-661) defaulting to None would let solo = no room, swarm = swarm-lounge.

Remove the hardcoded `"swarm-lounge" ::` prefix in the broker register/confirm announcement (c2c_identity_handlers.ml:349, c2c_broker.ml:4073) so the broker core stops presuming a universal social room — announce only into rooms actually joined.

Stop installing the git-pre-reset shim in default `install self`; make it `c2c install git-shim` opt-in (uninstall already treats git-shim as a separate component). The shim's entire reason-for-being is multi-agent main-tree contention.
Invert the kickoff/restart-intro default to a neutral 1:1 message; the override plumbing (swarm_config_restart_intro, [swarm] restart_intro) already exists — just swap which side is the default.
Make `prompt_for_role` opt-in (don't prompt by default) and change the kimi approval fallback + doctor text away from the literal 'coordinator1'.
Lead the README with a 2-agent 1:1 example before any swarm-lounge/coordinator content; move swarm onboarding to a clearly-labeled 'Swarm mode' section.
open_questions: Does the project want a single global mode flag (solo vs swarm) or finer-grained per-feature opt-ins? A mode flag is simpler but coarser; per-feature toggles already partly exist (e.g. --room '', [swarm] restart_intro).

Is the broker's unconditional swarm-lounge `peer_register` announcement relied upon anywhere for presence/discovery (e.g. does any agent watch swarm-lounge for joins)? If so, removing the hardcoded prepend needs a presence-event replacement; if not, it's pure dead weight for solo.

Should `install self` ever auto-install the git shim, or only when a swarm/coordinator context is detected? Need to confirm no other code path hard-requires the shim being present (uninstall lists it as optional, suggesting not).

The C2C_AUTO_JOIN_ROLE_ROOM="1" env is written to all clients but only consumed in c2c_start.ml build_env (managed-start path), gated on a role file existing — is it ever consumed by the MCP server directly? Grep shows no MCP-server consumer, so it appears inert for non-role solo use and could simply be dropped from the install defaults.

Are the role templates (role_templates.ml / role_designer_embedded.ml) intended to be generic or are they explicitly THIS dev-swarm's onboarding? If generic, the named peers (Cairn-Vigil, stanza-coder, coordinator1) and peer-PASS gate need extracting into a per-team profile.

dimension: Surface area: MCP tools, CLI command groups, env vars, config files — coupling to roles/coordinator
summary: c2c exposes 38 base MCP tools (+1 dev-only `debug`) and ~83 top-level CLI command entries. The MCP surface is almost entirely role-agnostic: `tools/list` returns the full static `tool_definitions` to every session unconditionally (ocaml/c2c_mcp.ml:430-432) — there is NO per-role or per-coordinator tool gating. The `role` field on `register` is stored and displayed but is NEVER read for any send/room/inbox routing decision (it is pure attribution metadata). The CLI does filter, but only on an agent-vs-operator axis (`is_agent_session()` = any session with `C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID` set; ocaml/cli/c2c_commands.ml:113-135) — not by role/coordinator. The coordinator concept couples in via exactly one env var, `C2C_COORDINATOR=1`, which is a privilege/guard-bypass flag (spoof-as-other-alias, worktree-mismatch-guard skip, main-tree commit allowance) plus the `coord` command group; it is opt-in and the whole mesh works without it. Structured-team surfaces (supervisor/approval/pending-reply permission flow, role-class pmodel table, role-room auto-join, hardcoded `coordinator1` defaults) are a cohesive but separable cluster bolted onto a role-agnostic core. The runbook env-var dictionary (~18 entries) is badly stale vs the ~90 distinct C2C_* vars actually read in code.

coupling_points.what_it_does: Every MCP session sees all 38 base tools (+debug in dev builds). tools/list returns the static tool_definitions list with no filtering by role, alias, or coordinator status.

dimension: Dead weight removal + irreducible role-agnostic core (1:1 peer messaging)
summary: The canonical OCaml binary already has a clean structural separation: the core messaging path (register -> send -> enqueue_message -> poll_inbox) is fully role-agnostic. The broker module (C2c_broker, ocaml/c2c_broker.ml) opens only C2c_mcp_helpers and never references C2c_role, Coord_fallthrough, or Relay_nudge; `role` is captured at register as a free-form optional string that is pure display metadata and never gates routing or delivery. The ONLY hard role coupling is `role.coordinator = Some true` -> `C2C_COORDINATOR=1` env (c2c_start.ml:4400), which is consumed solely by the git-shim guards (git-shim.sh) and the worktree-mismatch warning (c2c_broker.ml:1134) — both opt-in safety theatre for a shared-tree swarm, not messaging. The strongest *swarm assumption baked into the role-agnostic broker* is the unconditional `"swarm-lounge" ::` prepend at registration (c2c_broker.ml:4073 and c2c_identity_handlers.ml:349) plus the always-on Relay_nudge swarm-flavored idle-nudge thread (server inner :537). Substantial dead weight exists at the repo edges: ~50 deprecated root Python scripts (superseded by OCaml subcommands), legacy `run-*-inst*` / `restart-*-self` launcher scripts (git-tracked, zero live callers), full `crush` client residue (deprecated, `c2c start crush` refuses but ~25 code sites remain), the unused `data/c2c_alias_words.txt` (only the deprecated Python registry reads it), and a DEAD `configure_claude_hook` in c2c_setup.ml:1006. None of these block carving out a solo/flat-mesh core.

coupling_points.title: swarm-lounge unconditionally auto-joined at every registration
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:4073 `List.sort_uniq String.compare ("swarm-lounge" :: auto_rooms)`; duplicated at ocaml/c2c_identity_handlers.ml:349
coupling_points.what_it_does: Every peer that confirms registration is force-subscribed to a room literally named swarm-lounge (a peer_register announcement is posted on its behalf), regardless of role, config, or whether the user wants a social channel. This is the social-layer north-star assumption leaking into the role-agnostic broker core.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Replace the hardcoded literal with a `swarm_config_social_room ()` thunk (the planned #318 helper, referenced but not yet implemented per c2c_start.mli:340) reading `.c2c/config.toml [swarm] social_room`. For a solo user, default to empty/none so no auto-room is created; structured teams opt in by setting the key. Removes the only role-agnostic-broker dependency on the social layer.

coupling_points.what_it_does: Translates a role-file boolean into an env var that bypasses the git destructive-op guards and the worktree-mismatch warning. The messaging broker's send/deliver path never reads it; it only governs git-safety guard rails for a shared-tree multi-agent layout.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: The env var and guards are already opt-in: with no role file and no git-shim installed, none of this code runs. For the solo/flat-mesh core, simply don't install the git-shim/pre-reset guard (they are separate `c2c install git-shim` components). Keep C2C_COORDINATOR purely as a guard-bypass escape hatch; it has no messaging semantics to remove.

coupling_points.title: Relay_nudge swarm-themed idle nudges started unconditionally
coupling_points.evidence: ocaml/server/c2c_mcp_server_inner.ml:537 `Relay_nudge.start_nudge_scheduler ... ()`; message bodies hardcode swarm framing at ocaml/relay_nudge.ml:20-25 ("check the swarm-lounge", "want to review a PR?")
coupling_points.what_it_does: A background Lwt thread DMs idle sessions every ~30min with swarm-coordination prompts. Runs in every MCP server instance, including a solo user's, injecting unsolicited 'grab a task / review a PR' messages.
coupling_points.decouple_approach: Gate `start_nudge_scheduler` behind a config flag (e.g. `[swarm] idle_nudges = true`, default false) or behind the same social-room presence. The default messages are already externalized to a JSON file (relay_nudge.ml ensure_default_messages), so a solo user could also empty them; cleanest is to not start the thread when no social room is configured.

MCP TOOL SURFACE (minimal): register, whoami, list, send, poll_inbox (ocaml/c2c_mcp.ml:30-57). These five deliver 'two of my agents can message each other' with zero role/coordinator/swarm concept. peek_inbox is a convenience superset of poll_inbox.

ENVELOPE + ENVELOPE FORMATTING: ocaml/c2c_wire_bridge.ml format_envelope / spool I/O (despite the legacy name) and C2c_mcp.format_c2c_envelope produce the canonical `<c2c event=... from=... to=...>body</c2c>` wire format. Role tag is optional.
